fil.description: Buns ng Shanghai na crackle ang ilalim: yeasted dough na binalot sa juicy pork filling, ipiprito hanggang crisp sa base tapos isteam para matapos, may sumasabog na masarap na sabaw sa bawat kagat.
ingredients: aspic ng baboy o manok, cubed
steps: Haluin ang flour, yeast, asukal at mainit-init na tubig hanggang maging smooth na dough, masahin for 10 minutes, tapos i-proof lang ng 30 minutes para manatiling medyo chewy imbes na fluffy.
Haluin ang ground pork sa soy sauces, sesame oil, luya at scallions, tapos ihalo ang chilled aspic cubes nang hindi masyadong durog.
Hatiin ang dough sa 12 piraso, patagin ang bawat isa hanggang maging disc, lagyan ng isang kutsarang sahog, tapos i-pleat isara sa taas.
Ayusin ang buns nang nakaharap pataas ang pleat sa well-oiled na non-stick pan, may espasyo sa pagitan ng bawat isa.
Iprito sa medium heat, hindi natatakpan, for 3-4 minutes hanggang golden ang ilalim.
Lagyan ng tubig hanggang umabot sa ikatlong bahagi ng taas ng buns, takpan, tapos isteam for 8-10 minutes hanggang maluto na ang dough.
Alisin ang takip, budburan ng sesame seeds at scallions, tapos lutuin ng final na 2-3 minutes hindi natatakpan hanggang matuyo ang tubig at maging crisp ulit ang ilalim.
tips: Puwedeng gawin isang araw bago ang aspic pero dapat fully chilled at firm na ito bago ihalo, kung hindi ay magiging runny ang sahog.
Hawakan nang dahan-dahan ang buns kapag napuno na — ang napunit na wrapper ang magpapatagas sa sabaw habang niluluto.
fil.kidNote: Hindi maanghang, pero sobrang init ng sahog kapag bagong luto — pahintuin muna ng ilang minuto ang buns at paalalahanan ang mga bata tungkol sa mainit na sabaw sa loob bago sila kumagat.
fil.nutritionNote: Mamantika ang pork filling at aspic at maalat ang soy seasoning, at nagdadagdag pa ng mantika ang pagprito, kaya ihain ito kasama ng plain vegetable soup imbes na mas maraming pritong side dish.

recipes.title: Pork and Shrimp Siu Mai
recipes.description: Open-topped steamed dumplings packed with a bouncy pork and shrimp filling and shiitake mushroom, topped with a fleck of carrot — a dim sum table essential.

ingredients.item: dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and diced

steps: Rehydrate the shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain and dice finely.
In a stand mixer or by hand, beat the ground pork with cornstarch, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, sesame oil, white pepper and salt for about 4-5 minutes until it turns pale and sticky.
Fold in the diced shrimp and mushrooms until evenly distributed.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each wrapper and gently squeeze the sides upward around the filling, leaving the top open.
Tap each dumpling on the counter to flatten the base and press a few flecks of minced carrot into the top.
Line a steamer basket with parchment or cabbage leaves, arrange the dumplings with space between them, and steam over simmering water for 9 minutes until the filling is firm and opaque.
Serve hot, straight from the steamer, with chili oil or soy-vinegar dip on the side.
tips: These freeze well uncooked — steam straight from frozen, adding 2-3 minutes to the steaming time.
recipes.kidNote: Not spicy on its own; keep any chili dipping sauce off to the side so kids can eat theirs plain.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pork, shrimp and oyster sauce add up to a fairly sodium-heavy snack; steaming at least keeps added fat low, so pair with plain rice or vegetables rather than more fried dim sum.

fil.description: Bukas-taas na steamed dumplings na puno ng bouncy pork and shrimp filling at shiitake mushroom, may piraso ng carrot sa taas — essential sa dim sum table.
ingredients: dried shiitake mushrooms, binabad at dinicing
steps: Ibabad ang shiitake mushrooms sa mainit-init na tubig for 20 minutes, tapos i-drain at i-dice nang pino.
Sa stand mixer o gamit ang kamay, batihin ang ground pork kasama ang cornstarch, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, sesame oil, white pepper at asin for mga 4-5 minutes hanggang maging maputla at malagkit.
Ihalo ang dinicing na hipon at mushrooms hanggang pantay ang pagkakalat.
Maglagay ng isang kutsarang sahog sa gitna ng bawat wrapper at dahan-dahang pisilin ang gilid paitaas palibot sa sahog, iwang bukas ang taas.
I-tap ang bawat dumpling sa counter para patagin ang base at maglagay ng kaunting minced carrot sa taas.

Ilatag ang parchment o dahon ng repolyo sa steamer basket, ayusin ang dumplings na may espasyo sa pagitan, tapos isteam sa mahinang kumukulong tubig for 9 minutes hanggang firm at opaque na ang sahog.
Ihaing mainit, diretso mula sa steamer, may chili oil o soy-vinegar dip sa gilid.
tips: Maganda itong i-freeze kapag hilaw pa — isteam mula frozen, dagdagan ng 2-3 minutes ang oras ng pagsi-steam.
fil.kidNote: Hindi maanghang mismo; itabi ang anumang chili dipping sauce sa gilid para makakain ang mga bata nang plain.
fil.nutritionNote: Medyo mataas sa sodium ang kombinasyon ng pork, hipon at oyster sauce; kahit papaano, mababa sa taba ito dahil steamed, kaya isabay sa plain rice o gulay imbes na sa mas maraming pritong dim sum.

recipes.title: Red-Braised Pork Belly
recipes.description: Pork belly blanched, caramelized in melted rock sugar, then slow-braised in soy sauce and Shaoxing wine until the fat turns glossy and spoon-tender — Shanghai's signature sweet-savory braise.

ingredients.item: skin-on pork belly, cut into 2cm cubes

ingredients.note: enough to mostly cover the pork; top up as needed

steps: Cut the pork belly into 2cm cubes, cover with water in a pot, and bring to a boil for 1 minute until the surface turns opaque. Drain and rinse to remove impurities.
Wipe out the pot. Over low heat, melt the rock sugar in the oil, swirling gently until it turns a light amber.
Add the blanched pork belly and raise the heat to medium; cook, stirring, until the pieces are lightly browned and coated in caramel.
Reduce the heat to low, pour in the Shaoxing wine, and let it bubble for 2 minutes to cook off the raw alcohol smell.
Stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and enough water to mostly cover the pork.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring every 10 minutes and topping up water if it runs dry, until the pork is fork-tender.
Uncover, raise the heat, and stir constantly until the sauce reduces to a thick, glossy coating on the pork.
Serve hot over steamed rice.
tips: Don't let the sugar go past light amber — burnt caramel turns the whole braise bitter.
Make it a day ahead: the flavor deepens overnight and the fat sets, so you can skim it before reheating.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pork belly is fat-forward and the braise is salt-heavy from two soy sauces, so serve modest portions alongside plain rice and a big plate of steamed or blanched greens to balance it.

fil.description: Pork belly na binlanch muna, tapos ka-caramelize sa melted rock sugar, then slow-braised sa toyo at Shaoxing wine hanggang maging glossy at spoon-tender ang taba — ito ang signature sweet-savory braise ng Shanghai.
ingredients: skin-on pork belly, hiwain into 2cm cubes
tubig, sapat lang para matakpan ang pork; dagdagan kung kailangan
steps: Hiwain ang pork belly into 2cm cubes, takpan ng tubig sa pot, at pakuluan for 1 minute hanggang maging opaque ang surface. I-drain at hugasan para maalis ang mga impurities.
Punasan ang pot. Sa low heat, i-melt ang rock sugar sa oil, i-swirl nang dahan-dahan hanggang maging light amber ang kulay.
Idagdag ang blanched pork belly at taasan ang heat to medium; lutuin, haluin, hanggang lightly browned ang mga piraso at naka-coat sa caramel.
Ibaba ang heat to low, ibuhos ang Shaoxing wine, at hayaang mag-bubble for 2 minutes para maalis ang raw alcohol smell.
Isama ang light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, at sapat na tubig para halos matakpan ang pork.
Takpan at i-simmer sa medium-low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour, haluin every 10 minutes at dagdagan ng tubig kung natutuyo, hanggang fork-tender na ang pork.
Alisin ang takip, taasan ang heat, at patuloy na haluin hanggang mag-reduce ang sauce into thick, glossy coating sa pork.
Ihain mainit over steamed rice.
tips: Huwag hayaang lumagpas sa light amber ang sugar — burnt caramel makakapapait sa buong braise.
Gawin isang araw before: lalim pa ang lasa overnight at nagse-set ang taba, para ma-skim mo before i-reheat.
fil.nutritionNote: Fat-forward ang pork belly at salty ang braise dahil sa two soy sauces, kaya ihain ng modest portions kasama ng plain rice at malaking plato ng steamed or blanched greens para ma-balance.

recipes.title: Salt and Pepper Squid
recipes.localTitle: Jiao Yan You Yu (椒盐鱿鱼)
recipes.description: Squid is marinated, dredged in a light flour coating and fried until crisp, then flash-tossed with garlic, ginger and chilli — a Cantonese restaurant favorite that is quick to make at home.
steps: Cut the squid into bite-sized pieces, score a light crosshatch on one side, and pat completely dry.
Toss the squid with Shaoxing wine and sesame oil and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok to 175°C (350°F).
Mix the flour and cornstarch on a plate, dredge the squid pieces to coat lightly, and shake off the excess.
Fry the squid in batches for 60-90 seconds until pale golden and just cooked through, then drain on a rack.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil from the wok, then stir-fry the garlic, ginger and chilli over high heat for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Return the squid to the wok, sprinkle with salt and white pepper, and toss for 30 seconds over high heat.
Serve immediately over rice while the coating is still crisp.
tips: Fry hot and fast — squid turns rubbery within a minute over heat, so pull it the moment the coating sets and turns pale gold.
Pat the squid bone-dry before dredging or the coating will slide off in the oil.
recipes.kidNote: The heat here is mild and mostly from black pepper, not chilli. Set aside the kids' portion before adding the sliced green chilli to the wok.
recipes.nutritionNote: This is a fried dish, so drain it well on a rack and pair it with a simple stir-fried green vegetable to balance the meal.

fil.description: Marinated na pusit, dinredge sa magaan na coating na flour tapos ipiprito hanggang crisp, saka isasabayan ng bawang, luya at sili — paborito sa Cantonese restaurant na madaling gawin sa bahay.
steps: Hiwain ang pusit sa bite-sized na piraso, kurutan nang bahagya ang isang gilid, tapos patuyuin nang husto.
Haluin ang pusit sa Shaoxing wine at sesame oil at hayaan itong itabi for 10 minutes.
Painitin ang mantika sa wok hanggang 175°C (350°F).
Haluin ang flour at cornstarch sa isang plato, i-dredge ang mga piraso ng pusit para mabalutan nang manipis, tapos i-shake ang sobra.
Iprito ang pusit nang batch-batch for 60-90 seconds hanggang maputlang golden at maluto lang, tapos i-drain sa rack.
Alisin ang halos lahat ng mantika sa wok, panatilihin lang ang 1 tablespoon, tapos igisa ang bawang, luya at sili sa high heat for 20 seconds hanggang umamoy masarap.
Ibalik ang pusit sa wok, budburan ng asin at white pepper, tapos haluin ng 30 seconds sa high heat.
Ihaing agad sa ibabaw ng kanin habang crisp pa ang coating.
tips: Iprito nang mainit at mabilis — nagiging rubbery ang pusit kapag mahigit isang minuto sa apoy, kaya alisin agad kapag pumuti na at nag-set na ang coating.
Patuyuin nang husto ang pusit bago i-dredge o matatanggal ang coating sa mantika.
fil.kidNote: Magaan lang ang anghang dito at galing pa sa black pepper, hindi sa sili. Itabi muna ang portion ng mga bata bago ilagay ang hiniwang berdeng sili sa wok.
fil.nutritionNote: Pritong ulam ito, kaya i-drain nang mabuti sa rack at isabay sa simpleng ginisang gulay para i-balance ang meal.

recipes.title: Scallion Pancakes
recipes.description: Flaky, oniony flatbread layered by rolling and coiling oiled dough into a spiral, then pan-frying until crisp outside and chewy within — a street-cart breakfast staple.

ingredients.note: or make traditional hot-water dough from 1.5 cups flour and 0.5 cup hot water

steps: Wash and dry the scallions thoroughly, then chop finely.
Stack 4-5 dumpling wrappers, brushing a little oil, a pinch of salt and a scattering of scallions between each layer.
Roll the stack out gently with a rolling pin into a thin, round pancake about 6 inches across; repeat to make 3 pancakes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a flat-bottomed pan over medium heat and fry a pancake for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Repeat with the remaining pancakes, adding oil as needed.
Stir together the soy sauce, vinegar and garlic for the dipping sauce, and cut each pancake into wedges to serve.
tips: Dry the scallions completely before layering — wet scallions steam the dough instead of letting it crisp.
recipes.kidNote: No spice; kids usually prefer these plain with just a dip of soy sauce rather than the vinegar-garlic mix.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pan-frying in oil makes this rich in fat; blot briefly on paper towels after cooking and serve it as a side rather than the whole meal.

fil.description: Flaky, may lasang sibuyas na flatbread na ginawa sa pag-roll at pag-coil ng oiled dough papunta sa spiral, tapos ipiprito hanggang crisp sa labas at chewy sa loob — street-cart breakfast staple.
steps: Hugasan at patuyuin nang mabuti ang scallions, tapos tadtarin nang pino.
I-stack ang 4-5 dumpling wrappers, pahiran ng kaunting mantika, dashing ng asin at budbog ng scallions sa pagitan ng bawat layer.
I-roll nang dahan-dahan ang stack gamit ang rolling pin hanggang maging manipis, bilog na pancake na mga 6 inches ang lapad; ulitin para makagawa ng 3 pancakes.
Painitin ang 1 tablespoon na mantika sa flat-bottomed pan sa medium heat at iprito ang isang pancake for 2-3 minutes per side hanggang golden at crisp.
Ulitin sa natitirang pancakes, magdagdag ng mantika kung kailangan.
Haluin ang soy sauce, suka at bawang para sa dipping sauce, tapos hiwain ang bawat pancake sa wedges bago ihain.
tips: Patuyuin nang husto ang scallions bago i-layer — ang basang scallions ang nagpapasteam sa dough instead na hayaan itong mag-crisp.
fil.kidNote: Walang anghang; mas gusto ng mga bata itong plain, dip lang sa soy sauce imbes na sa vinegar-garlic mix.
fil.nutritionNote: Mamantika ito dahil sa pagprito; i-blot lang nang kaunti sa paper towel pagkatapos lutuin at ihain bilang side dish imbes na buong meal.

recipes.title: Shrimp Dumplings
recipes.description: Delicate, translucent wheat-starch dumplings pleated tight around a juicy whole-shrimp and bamboo shoot filling — the benchmark dish dim sum cooks are judged by.

ingredients.item: raw shrimp, peeled and roughly chopped

steps: Mix the shrimp with oyster sauce, sesame oil, white pepper, ginger, salt and sugar; fold in the bamboo shoots and chill while making the dough.
Whisk the wheat starch and cornstarch together, then pour in the boiling water all at once, stirring rapidly until it forms a shaggy, translucent mass.
Add the lard and knead the hot dough until smooth, keeping it covered with a damp towel between steps so it doesn't dry out.
Roll the dough into a log and divide into 18 equal pieces, flattening each into a thin round with the flat side of an oiled cleaver or a small rolling pin.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each wrapper and pleat one edge around the other, sealing into a crescent shape.
Line a steamer with parchment, arrange the dumplings with space between them, and steam over high heat for 6 minutes until translucent.
Serve immediately — har gow does not reheat well, so time the steaming for right before eating.
tips: The water must be fully boiling when you pour it into the starch, or the dough won't turn translucent and will crack when rolled.
If the wrapper cracks while rolling, it's too dry — knead in a few drops of hot water and keep unused dough covered.
Expect the wrapping to take practice; even experienced dim sum cooks spend a long time getting the pleating even.
recipes.kidNote: Not spicy and easy for kids to eat; just watch that the shrimp filling is cooked through and fully opaque before serving.
recipes.nutritionNote: Steaming keeps this genuinely low in added fat, though the filling is seasoned with oyster sauce and sesame oil for sodium — one of the lighter dim sum choices in this batch.

fil.description: Manipis, translucent na wheat-starch dumplings na mahigpit ang pleating sa paligid ng juicy whole-shrimp at bamboo shoot filling — ang dish na pinagbabatayan ng husay ng dim sum cooks.
ingredients: hilaw na hipon, balat na at tinadtad
steps: Haluin ang hipon sa oyster sauce, sesame oil, white pepper, luya, asin at asukal; ihalo ang bamboo shoots at palamigin habang ginagawa ang dough.
Haluin ang wheat starch at cornstarch, tapos ibuhos ang kumukulong tubig nang sabay-sabay, haluin nang mabilis hanggang maging shaggy, translucent na masa.
Idagdag ang lard at masahin ang mainit na dough hanggang smooth, panatilihing natatakpan ng damp towel sa pagitan ng steps para hindi matuyo.
I-roll ang dough papunta sa log at hatiin sa 18 pantay na piraso, patagin ang bawat isa hanggang maging manipis na bilog gamit ang patag na gilid ng oiled cleaver o maliit na rolling pin.
Maglagay ng isang kutsarang sahog sa gitna ng bawat wrapper at i-pleat ang isang gilid papalibot sa kabila, isara papunta sa hugis crescent.
Ilatag ang parchment sa steamer, ayusin ang dumplings na may espasyo sa pagitan, tapos isteam sa mataas na apoy for 6 minutes hanggang maging translucent.
Ihaing agad — hindi maganda i-reheat ang har gow, kaya i-time ang pagsi-steam bago mismo kainin.
tips: Dapat fully boiling ang tubig kapag ibinuhos sa starch, kung hindi ay hindi magiging translucent ang dough at mapuputol pag i-roll.
Kung napupunit ang wrapper habang ni-ro-roll, masyado itong tuyo — masahan ng kaunting patak ng mainit na tubig at itago ang natitirang dough na natatakpan.
Asahang mangangailangan ito ng practice; kahit experienced na dim sum cooks ay matagal bago maging pantay ang pleating.
fil.kidNote: Hindi maanghang at madaling kainin ng mga bata; siguraduhin lang na maluto nang husto at opaque na ang hipon bago ihain.
fil.nutritionNote: Mababa talaga sa added fat ito dahil steamed, kahit may sodium ang sahog dahil sa oyster sauce at sesame oil — isa ito sa pinaka-magaan na choice ng dim sum sa batch na ito.

recipes.title: Shrimp with Scrambled Egg
recipes.localTitle: Hua Dan Xia Ren (滑蛋虾仁)
recipes.description: Shrimp seared just until pink and folded into soft, glossy scrambled eggs off the heat — a fast Cantonese home-style plate that turns two humble ingredients into something silky.
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp, then pat dry. Season with salt and white pepper, then toss in the cornstarch last so it coats the surface without diluting into the shrimp.
Let the shrimp sit for 10 minutes while you beat the eggs with a little oil, salt and sugar.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sear the shrimp for about 1 minute per side until just pink and curled; remove and set aside — they'll finish cooking with the eggs.
Wipe out the wok, add a little more oil, and pour in the beaten eggs.
Let the bottom set for about 10 seconds, then use a spatula to fold the cooked layer over so uncooked egg flows underneath; repeat for about 30 seconds total.
Fold the shrimp back into the eggs, turn off the heat, and let the residual heat finish setting the eggs into soft, glossy curds, about 15-20 more seconds.
Scatter with scallion and serve immediately over rice.
tips: Season the shrimp with salt and pepper first and add the cornstarch last — it coats better and gives a cleaner sear than mixing everything at once.
Turn the heat off before the eggs look fully set; they keep cooking in the residual heat of the wok and firm up too much if you wait for that on the stove.
recipes.nutritionNote: A lean, high-protein, low-carb plate on its own, good for balancing out a heavier dish like sweet and sour pork on the same table — just pair with rice or a vegetable side since it has no fiber of its own.

fil.description: Hipon na sini-sear lang hanggang pink at hinalo sa soft at glossy scrambled eggs, patay na ang apoy — mabilis na Cantonese home-style plate na ginagawang silky ang dalawang simpleng ingredients.
ingredients: hipon, balatan at alisan ng ugat
steps: Balatan at alisan ng ugat ang hipon, tapos punasan hanggang matuyo. I-season ng asin at white pepper, tapos idagdag ang cornstarch huling-huli para ma-coat ang surface na hindi lumusaw sa hipon.
Hayaang maupo ang hipon for 10 minutes habang binibitin ang itlog with kaunting oil, asin at asukal.
Painitin ang oil sa wok sa high heat at i-sear ang hipon for about 1 minute per side hanggang just pink at naka-curl; alisin at itabi — matatapos ang pagluluto nila kasama ng itlog.
Punasan ang wok, magdagdag ng kaunting oil, at ibuhos ang binitin na itlog.
Hayaang mag-set ang ilalim for about 10 seconds, tapos gamitin ang spatula para i-fold ang cooked layer para dumaloy ang uncooked egg sa ilalim; ulitin for about 30 seconds total.
I-fold ang hipon pabalik sa itlog, patayin ang apoy, at hayaang tapusin ng residual heat ang pag-set ng itlog into soft at glossy curds, about 15-20 more seconds.
Budburan ng scallion at ihain agad over rice.
tips: I-season muna ng asin at pepper ang hipon tapos idagdag ang cornstarch huli — mas maganda ang coating at mas malinis ang sear kaysa haluin lahat nang sabay.
Patayin ang apoy bago pa fully set ang itlog; tuloy pa rin ang pagluluto nila sa residual heat ng wok at magiging masyadong matigas kung hihintayin mo pa sa kalan.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean, high-protein at low-carb na plate ito on its own, maganda para i-balance ang mas mabigat na dish gaya ng sweet and sour pork sa parehong table — isabay lang sa kanin o vegetable side dahil walang fiber ang dish mismo.

recipes.title: Soy Sauce Chicken
recipes.description: A whole chicken gently poached in a spiced soy sauce master stock until just cooked through, then bathed in the cooling liquid for silky, deeply seasoned meat and glossy amber skin — Cantonese roast-meat-shop cooking at home.

ingredients.note: for brushing the skin at the end

steps: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking so it isn't cold going into the pot.

Heat the oil in a pot just large enough to hold the chicken. Add the ginger and scallion and cook over medium-low heat until fragrant and lightly caramelized, about 1 minute, then add the star anise and cinnamon.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine and let it bubble 1 minute, then add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar and water. Bring to a simmer and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Lower the whole chicken breast-side down into the simmering sauce; it should be at least two-thirds submerged. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes.

Flip the chicken breast-side up, cover, and simmer another 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and let the chicken sit in the hot sauce, covered, for 20 minutes to finish cooking through without drying out.
Check doneness by piercing the thickest part of the thigh — the juices should run clear with no pink. Lift the chicken out and brush the skin with sesame oil for shine.
Rest 10 minutes, then chop into pieces and spoon some of the sauce over the top to serve.
Strain and save the remaining sauce; it keeps in the fridge for weeks and can be reused as a master stock for the next batch.
tips: Turning off the heat and letting the chicken finish in the residual heat of the sauce, rather than simmering it the whole time, is what keeps the breast meat silky instead of stringy.
Save the strained master sauce — each reuse gets more complex, and it's the traditional way this dish is made in Cantonese homes.
recipes.nutritionNote: The poaching method needs almost no added fat, but the sauce itself is concentrated soy and salty even diluted with water, so spoon it sparingly over the meat and serve with plain rice and a vegetable side rather than more sauce at the table.

fil.description: Isang whole chicken na dahan-dahang pinoach sa spiced soy sauce master stock hanggang cooked through lang, tapos ibinabad sa cooling liquid para maging silky at deeply seasoned ang karne at glossy amber ang balat — Cantonese roast-meat-shop cooking sa bahay.
ingredients: sesame oil, for brushing sa balat sa dulo
steps: Ilabas ang manok sa fridge 30 minutes bago magluto para hindi malamig kapag inilagay sa pot.

Painitin ang oil sa pot na sapat kalaki para sa manok. Idagdag ang luya at scallion at lutuin sa medium-low heat hanggang umamoy masarap at bahagyang mag-caramelize, about 1 minute, tapos idagdag ang star anise at cinnamon.
Ibuhos ang Shaoxing wine at hayaang mag-bubble for 1 minute, tapos idagdag ang light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar at tubig. I-simmer at haluin hanggang matunaw ang asukal.
Ibaba ang whole chicken nang paharap sa ilalim ang breast sa simmering sauce; dapat two-thirds submerged at least. Takpan at i-simmer nang mahinay for 15 minutes.

Baliktarin ang manok nang paharap sa itaas ang breast, takpan, at i-simmer ulit for 15 minutes, tapos patayin ang apoy at hayaang mag-sit ang manok sa mainit na sauce, nakatakip, for 20 minutes para matapos maluto nang tuluyan nang hindi natutuyo.
I-check ang doneness sa pagtusok sa pinakamakapal na parte ng hita — dapat malinaw ang tumutulong juice, walang pink. Buhatin ang manok at pahiran ang balat ng sesame oil para kumintab.
Ipahinga for 10 minutes, tapos hiwain into pieces at ibuhos ang kaunti sa sauce sa ibabaw bago ihain.
I-strain at itago ang natitirang sauce; tumatagal ito sa fridge for weeks at pwedeng gamitin ulit as master stock for the next batch.
tips: Ang pagpatay ng apoy at pagpapatapos sa manok gamit ang residual heat ng sauce, instead of i-simmer nang buong oras, ang dahilan kung bakit silky ang breast meat imbes na stringy.
Itago ang na-strain na master sauce — mas complex ang lasa kada gamit ulit, at ito ang traditional way ng dish na ito sa mga Cantonese home.
fil.nutritionNote: Halos walang added fat na kailangan ang poaching method, pero concentrated soy at maalat pa rin ang sauce kahit may tubig na, kaya ibuhos nang konti lang over the meat at ihain with plain rice at vegetable side instead of dagdag pang sauce sa table.

recipes.title: Steamed BBQ Pork Buns
recipes.description: Pillowy white steamed buns split open to reveal a sweet-savoury diced char siu pork filling in a glossy oyster sauce gravy — the dim sum cart favourite.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in warm water, then mix with the flour, cornstarch, sugar and oil into a smooth dough; cover and let rise 2 hours until doubled.
Meanwhile, sauté the shallots in oil until fragrant, add the oyster sauce, soy sauces and stock, and simmer with the flour whisked in until thickened.
Stir the diced char siu into the sauce, coat well, then cool completely in the fridge.
Knead the baking powder into the risen dough, then rest a further 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 10 pieces, flatten into discs, spoon in the cooled filling, and pleat closed at the top.
Set each bun on a square of parchment and rest 15 minutes before steaming.
Steam over high heat in batches for 12 minutes until puffed and glossy white; let the buns rest 2 minutes before opening the lid.
tips: Cool the filling fully before wrapping — warm filling softens the dough and makes it hard to seal.
recipes.kidNote: Not spicy; the sweet-savoury filling is one of the easiest dim sum items for kids to like.
recipes.nutritionNote: The oyster and soy sauces make the filling fairly salty, and the dough itself has added sugar and oil; balance the meal with steamed greens rather than more fried dim sum.

fil.description: Malambot na puting steamed buns na pag-bukas ay lalabasan ng sweet-savoury na dinicing char siu pork filling na nasa glossy oyster sauce gravy — paborito sa dim sum cart.
steps: Tunawin ang yeast sa mainit-init na tubig, tapos ihalo sa flour, cornstarch, asukal at mantika hanggang maging smooth na dough; takpan at hayaang mag-rise for 2 hours hanggang doble na ang laki.
Samantala, igisa ang shallots sa mantika hanggang umamoy masarap, idagdag ang oyster sauce, soy sauces at stock, tapos i-simmer kasama ng flour na hinalo hanggang lumapot.
Ihalo ang dinicing char siu sa sauce, balutin nang mabuti, tapos palamigin nang husto sa fridge.
Masahin ang baking powder papunta sa risen dough, tapos itabi muna another 15 minutes.
Hatiin ang dough sa 10 piraso, patagin hanggang maging discs, lagyan ng palamig na sahog, tapos i-pleat isara sa taas.
Ilagay ang bawat bun sa piraso ng parchment at itabi muna for 15 minutes bago isteam.
Isteam sa high heat nang batch-batch for 12 minutes hanggang lumaki at maging glossy white; hayaang magpahinga ang buns ng 2 minutes bago buksan ang takip.
tips: Palamigin nang husto ang sahog bago balutin — ang mainit na sahog ang nagpapalambot sa dough at nagpapahirap sa pagsasara nito.
fil.kidNote: Hindi maanghang; isa ito sa pinakamadaling dim sum item na magugustuhan ng mga bata dahil sa sweet-savoury na sahog.
fil.nutritionNote: Medyo maalat ang sahog dahil sa oyster at soy sauces, at may extra asukal at mantika ang dough mismo; i-balance ang meal ng steamed greens imbes na mas maraming pritong dim sum.

recipes.title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
recipes.description: A whole fish steamed just until the flesh flakes, doused in a sizzling hot oil over ginger and scallion — the centerpiece of a Cantonese family dinner and proof the simplest method is the hardest to get right.

ingredients.item: whole tilapia or sea bass, cleaned and scored
ginger, half julienned and half sliced

steps: Pat the fish dry and score the thickest part of the flesh a few times so it cooks evenly. Tuck a few ginger slices under the fish on the plate to keep it off the pooling liquid.
Scatter half the julienned ginger and scallion over the fish.

Set up a steamer with plenty of water at a rolling boil. Lower the fish in on its plate, cover, and steam over high heat for 10-12 minutes until the thickest part is opaque and the eyes have turned white.
While the fish steams, combine the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, water, sugar and salt in a small saucepan and bring to a brief simmer; keep warm.
Carefully lift the fish out, tilt the plate to drain off the cloudy steaming liquid, and discard it — this liquid tastes fishy and would ruin the sauce.
Top the fish with the remaining fresh ginger, scallion and cilantro, then pour the warm seasoned sauce over it.
Heat the neutral oil and sesame oil in a small pan until just shimmering and starting to smoke, then carefully pour it over the scallions and ginger — it should sizzle loudly and wilt them instantly.
Serve immediately straight from the plate.
tips: Buy the freshest fish you can — with only ginger, scallion and soy sauce, there's nowhere for off flavors to hide.
Don't skip draining the steaming liquid before saucing; it carries the fishy smell and would make the whole plate taste muddy.
recipes.nutritionNote: A lean white fish steamed with almost no added fat until the final oil drizzle — the lightest main in the rotation, so pair it with a starchier side like fried rice to round out the meal.

fil.description: Isang buong isda na sini-steam lang hanggang mag-flake ang laman, binuhusan ng sizzling hot oil sa ibabaw ng luya at scallion — ang centerpiece ng Cantonese family dinner at patunay na ang pinakasimpleng technique ang pinakamahirap gawin nang tama.
ingredients: buong tilapia o sea bass, nilinis at may guhit
luya, half julienned at half hiwain
steps: Punasan ang isda hanggang matuyo at guhitan ang pinakamakapal na parte ng laman nang ilang beses para pantay ang pagkaluto. Ilagay ang ilang hiwa ng luya sa ilalim ng isda sa plato para hindi ito matakpan ng natitirang tubig.
Isabog ang half ng julienned na luya at scallion sa ibabaw ng isda.

Ihanda ang steamer na maraming tubig at nasa rolling boil. Ibaba ang isda kasama ang plato nito, takpan, at i-steam sa high heat for 10-12 minutes hanggang opaque na ang pinakamakapal na parte at puti na ang mata.
Habang niluluto ang isda, i-combine ang light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, tubig, asukal at asin sa maliit na saucepan at pakuluan nang bahagya; panatilihing mainit.
Dahan-dahang buhatin ang isda, ikiling ang plato para matanggal ang cloudy steaming liquid, tapos itapon ito — mabaho ito at masisira ang sauce.
Ilagay sa ibabaw ng isda ang natitirang sariwang luya, scallion at cilantro, tapos ibuhos ang mainit na seasoned sauce dito.

Painitin ang neutral oil at sesame oil sa maliit na kawali hanggang shimmering at halos umuusok, tapos dahan-dahang ibuhos ito sa scallions at luya — dapat sumingasing nang malakas at agad malanta ang mga ito.
Ihain agad diretso sa plato.
tips: Bumili ng pinakasariwang isda na makakaya mo — sa ginger, scallion at soy sauce lang, walang matataguan ang off flavors.
Huwag laktawan ang pag-drain ng steaming liquid before i-sauce; mabaho ito at masisira ang lasa ng buong plato.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean white fish na sini-steam with almost no added fat hanggang sa final oil drizzle — ang pinaka-light na main sa rotation, kaya isabay sa starchier side gaya ng fried rice para kumpleto ang meal.

recipes.title: Steamed Minced Pork with Salted Egg
recipes.localTitle: Xian Dan Zheng Rou Bing (咸蛋蒸肉饼)
recipes.description: Ground pork is whipped with ginger and seasonings into a smooth paste, topped with salted duck egg yolks, and steamed into a savory patty that turns its own juices into a rice-soaking sauce.

ingredients.item: raw salted duck eggs, yolks and whites separated

steps: Combine the ground pork, ginger, cornstarch, sugar, white pepper, oyster sauce, water, sesame oil and the reserved salted egg whites in a shallow heatproof dish.
Mix vigorously with chopsticks in one direction for 2-3 minutes until the mixture turns pale and smooth, almost like a paste — this emulsifying is what keeps the patty tender.
Spread the mixture evenly across the dish so it cooks through at the same rate.
Halve the salted egg yolks and arrange them, cut side up, over the surface of the pork.
Set the dish into a steamer over boiling water, cover, and steam for 18-20 minutes until the pork is just cooked through and the juices run clear.
Rest, covered, off the heat for 5 minutes before uncovering.
Scatter with scallions and serve straight from the dish with plenty of steamed rice to soak up the juices.
tips: Mixing the pork in one direction until it turns pale and sticky is what makes the finished patty smooth rather than crumbly.
Covering the dish while it rests off the heat lets the residual steam finish the centre gently without overcooking the edges.
recipes.nutritionNote: Salted duck egg adds significant sodium, so no extra salt is needed in the mix; pair this with a plain blanched or stir-fried vegetable to round out the meal.

fil.description: Binabatilis ang ground pork kasama ng luya at pampalasa hanggang maging smooth na paste, tinatapunan ng salted duck egg yolks, tapos isasteam papunta sa savory patty na ginagawang rice-soaking sauce ang sarili nitong sabaw.
ingredients: hilaw na salted duck eggs, hiwalay ang puti at pula
steps: Haluin ang ground pork, luya, cornstarch, asukal, white pepper, oyster sauce, tubig, sesame oil at ang natirang puti ng salted egg sa isang mababaw na heatproof dish.

Haluin nang masigla gamit ang chopsticks sa iisang direksyon for 2-3 minutes hanggang maputla at maging smooth ang timpla, halos parang paste — itong pag-emulsify ang nagpapanatiling malambot ng patty.
Ikalat nang pantay ang timpla sa buong dish para pantay ang pagkaluto nito.
Hatiin sa kalahati ang mga salted egg yolks at ayusin, nakaharap pataas ang hiwa, sa ibabaw ng pork.
Ilagay ang dish sa steamer sa ibabaw ng kumukulong tubig, takpan, tapos isteam for 18-20 minutes hanggang maluto na ang pork at malinaw na ang tumutulong sabaw.
Ipahinga, natatakpan, malayo sa apoy for 5 minutes bago buksan ang takip.
Budburan ng scallions tapos ihaing diretso mula sa dish na may sagana kanin para hitin ang sabaw.
tips: Ang paghalo sa pork sa iisang direksyon hanggang maputla at malagkit ang nagpapanatiling smooth ng natapos na patty imbes na crumbly.
Ang pagtakip sa dish habang nagpapahinga malayo sa apoy ang nagpapahintulot sa natirang init na tapusin nang dahan-dahan ang gitna nang walang overcooking sa gilid.
fil.nutritionNote: Nagdadagdag ng malaking sodium ang salted duck egg, kaya hindi na kailangan ng extra asin sa timpla; isabay ito sa plain na blinanch o ginisang gulay para maging kumpleto ang meal.

recipes.title: Steamed Pork Ribs with Black Bean Sauce
recipes.localTitle: Chi Zhi Zheng Pai Gu (豉汁蒸排骨)
recipes.description: Small pork rib pieces are marinated with fermented black beans, garlic and a touch of cornstarch, then steamed until juicy — the dish everyone reaches for first off the dim sum cart.

ingredients.item: fermented black beans, rinsed and roughly chopped

steps: Soak the rib pieces in cold water for 10 minutes to draw out bone fragments and blood, then drain and pat dry.
Combine the black beans, garlic, sugar, salt, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil and white pepper in a bowl and mix into the ribs.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes, or overnight for deeper flavor.
Stir the cornstarch and water into the marinated ribs just before steaming so the sauce clings and thickens.
Spread the ribs in a single layer on a heatproof plate with a lip to catch the juices.
Set the plate into a steamer over boiling water and steam for 18-20 minutes until the ribs are fully cooked and tender.
Scatter with sliced red chilli and serve straight from the steaming plate with rice.
tips: Ask the butcher to chop the ribs small, or use kitchen shears — smaller pieces steam through faster and evenly.
recipes.nutritionNote: Ribs carry more fat than lean pork cuts, so serve with plenty of steamed vegetables or a light soup to round out the meal.

fil.description: Maliit na piraso ng pork ribs ang niratang-marinate sa fermented black beans, bawang at kaunting cornstarch, tapos isteam hanggang juicy — ang unang hahablutin sa dim sum cart.
ingredients: pork ribs, hinawa sa 1-inch na piraso
fermented black beans, banlawan at tadtarin nang bahagya
steps: Ibabad ang mga piraso ng ribs sa malamig na tubig for 10 minutes para mahugot ang butil ng buto at dugo, tapos i-drain at patuyuin.
Haluin ang black beans, bawang, asukal, asin, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil at white pepper sa isang bowl tapos ihalo sa ribs.
Takpan at i-marinate sa fridge nang at least 30 minutes, o overnight para mas malalim ang lasa.
Haluin ang cornstarch at tubig papunta sa naratang ribs bago mismo isteam para dumikit at lumapot ang sauce.
Ikalat ang ribs nang isang layer sa heatproof plate na may lip para masalo ang tumutulong sabaw.
Ilagay ang plate sa steamer sa ibabaw ng kumukulong tubig at isteam for 18-20 minutes hanggang maluto nang husto at malambot ang ribs.
Budburan ng hiniwang pulang sili at ihaing diretso mula sa steaming plate na may kanin.
tips: Pahingin sa butcher na durugin nang maliliit ang ribs, o gumamit ng kitchen shears — mas mabilis at pantay maluto ang mas maliliit na piraso.
fil.nutritionNote: Mas mataba ang ribs kumpara sa lean cuts ng pork, kaya ihain ito kasama ng maraming steamed vegetables o magaan na sabaw para i-round out ang meal.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Bok Choy with Mushrooms
recipes.description: Baby bok choy and shiitake mushrooms stir-fried hot and fast with garlic, then glazed with oyster sauce — the everyday vegetable side that shows up on nearly every Cantonese family dinner table.

ingredients.item: baby bok choy, halved or quartered lengthwise

steps: Wash the bok choy thoroughly, since dirt hides in the base, and halve or quarter each head lengthwise.
Stir together the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and water or stock in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering, then add the garlic and stir-fry 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry 2 minutes until they soften and start to brown at the edges.
Add the bok choy and stir-fry 1-2 minutes until the leaves wilt and the stems turn bright green but stay crisp.
Pour in the sauce, toss for 30 seconds until it reduces to a light glaze coating the vegetables, then drizzle in the sesame oil.
Serve immediately while the bok choy is still crisp-tender.
tips: Cook the bok choy stems and leaves together but keep the total time short — overcooked bok choy turns watery and loses its bite.
Fresh shiitakes give more texture than dried here since the vegetable itself is the point, not a rehydrated mushroom flavor base.
recipes.nutritionNote: A genuinely low-oil, high-fiber vegetable side; the oyster sauce is the only sodium source, so this pairs well alongside a saltier main like char siu or soy sauce chicken without pushing the whole meal over on salt.

fil.description: Baby bok choy at shiitake mushrooms na na-stir-fry nang mabilis at mainit with bawang, tapos na-glaze ng oyster sauce — everyday na vegetable side na lumalabas sa halos lahat ng Cantonese family dinner table.
ingredients: baby bok choy, hatiin o quarter-in nang lengthwise
steps: Hugasan nang mabuti ang bok choy, dahil nagtatago ang dumi sa base, at hatiin o quarter-in ang bawat head nang lengthwise.
Ihalo ang oyster sauce, toyo, asukal at tubig o stock sa maliit na mangkok.
Painitin ang oil sa wok sa high heat hanggang shimmering, tapos idagdag ang bawang at i-stir-fry for 10 seconds hanggang umamoy masarap.
Idagdag ang mushrooms at i-stir-fry for 2 minutes hanggang lumambot at magsimulang mag-brown sa gilid.
Idagdag ang bok choy at i-stir-fry for 1-2 minutes hanggang malanta ang dahon at maging bright green ang tangkay pero crisp pa rin.
Ibuhos ang sauce, haluin for 30 seconds hanggang lumapot into light glaze na coating sa gulay, tapos lagyan ng sesame oil.
Ihain agad habang crisp-tender pa ang bok choy.
tips: Lutuin nang sabay ang tangkay at dahon ng bok choy pero panatilihing maikli ang total time — kapag overcooked ang bok choy, nagiging watery ito at nawawala ang bite.
Mas maraming texture ang fresh shiitakes kaysa sa dried dito dahil ang gulay mismo ang punto, hindi rehydrated na mushroom flavor base.
fil.nutritionNote: Genuinely low-oil at high-fiber na vegetable side; ang oyster sauce lang ang sodium source, kaya maganda itong i-pair with mas maalat na main gaya ng char siu o soy sauce chicken nang hindi masyadong tumataas ang asin ng buong meal.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Pea Shoots with Garlic
recipes.localTitle: Suan Rong Chao Dou Miao (蒜蓉炒豆苗)
recipes.description: Tender pea shoot leaves are flash stir-fried with plenty of garlic over high heat for barely a minute — a delicate, quick vegetable dish prized at Chinese banquets and home tables alike.
steps: Rinse the pea shoots and spin or pat them completely dry — any water left on the leaves will make the stir-fry steam instead of sear.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until it just starts to shimmer.
Add the garlic and stir for a few seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the pea shoots all at once and stir-fry constantly for about 20 seconds, keeping the leaves moving.
Add salt and white pepper and continue tossing for another 30-40 seconds until the leaves are wilted but still bright green.
Drizzle in the sesame oil, toss once more, and serve immediately.
tips: Have every ingredient measured and next to the wok before you start — this dish is done in under a minute of actual cooking.
Use a wide wok and high heat so the leaves wilt rather than stew in their own liquid.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pea shoots are high in vitamins A and C and cook in minimal oil; this pairs naturally with any of the braised pork or beef dishes for a balanced plate.

fil.description: Malambot na dahon ng pea shoots ang flash stir-fried kasama ng maraming bawang sa high heat sa loob lang ng isang minuto — mabilis, delikado na gulay na paborito sa Chinese banquets at home table.
ingredients: pea shoots, tinanggalan ng matitigas na tangkay
steps: Banlawan ang pea shoots at i-spin o patuyuin nang husto — anumang tubig na natira sa dahon ay magpapasteam sa stir-fry imbes na mag-sear.
Painitin ang mantika sa wok sa high heat hanggang shimmering lang.
Idagdag ang bawang at haluin nang ilang segundo hanggang umamoy masarap pero hindi pa naka-brown.
Idagdag ang pea shoots nang sabay-sabay tapos igisa nang tuloy-tuloy for mga 20 seconds, panatilihing gumagalaw ang dahon.
Idagdag ang asin at white pepper tapos haluin pa ng 30-40 seconds hanggang malanta ang dahon pero bright green pa rin.
Patakan ng sesame oil, haluin ulit, tapos ihaing agad.
tips: Ihanda at sukatin muna ang lahat ng sahog malapit sa wok bago simulan — sub-isang minuto lang ang actual na pagluluto nito.
Gumamit ng malapad na wok at high heat para malanta lang ang dahon instead na maluto sa sarili nitong likido.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa vitamins A at C ang pea shoots at niluluto sa kaunting mantika lang; naturally bagay ito sa alinman sa mga braised pork o beef dishes para sa balanced na plato.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Pork
recipes.description: Pork double-fried until shatteringly crisp, then tossed in a ketchup-and-vinegar sauce simmered slowly with star anise until glossy — the dish that makes even reluctant vegetable-avoiders happy at the table.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder or tenderloin, cut into bite-sized chunks

ingredients.note: reserve 1 tsp for the sauce-thickening slurry
about 1 liter, or enough to submerge the pork

ingredients.item: green bell pepper, cut into 3cm squares

steps: Toss the pork with the marinade (water, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic powder and onion powder) until no liquid remains; set aside for 30 minutes.

Make the sauce base: heat oil in a small saucepan, add the ginger and star anise, and cook until fragrant and lightly caramelized, about 1 minute. Add the ketchup and stir until it darkens slightly, about 2 minutes.
Add the vinegar, sugar and reserved pineapple juice. Simmer uncovered on low heat, stirring occasionally, for about 30 minutes until the sauce is glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Heat the deep-frying oil to 175°C (350°F). Dredge the marinated pork in the flour-cornstarch mixture, dip in the beaten egg, then dredge again.
Fry the pork in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain. Just before serving, re-fry all the pork for 30-60 seconds to make it extra crisp.
Stir-fry the bell pepper and onion in a splash of oil over high heat for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sweet and sour sauce and the pineapple chunks; simmer to thicken, adding a little of the reserved cornstarch mixed with water if it needs to tighten further.
Add the crispy pork, toss quickly to coat without letting it sit in the sauce, and serve immediately so it stays crunchy.
tips: Fry the pork twice: once to cook it through, then a fast second fry right before saucing — that's what keeps it crunchy under the sauce instead of going soggy.
Toss the fried pork into the sauce only right before serving; sauced pork left to sit loses its crunch fast.
recipes.nutritionNote: This is the richest dish in the rotation, deep-fried batter plus a sugar-and-ketchup sauce, so treat it as an occasional treat, serve smaller portions alongside plenty of plain rice and a green vegetable, and skip other fried or sweet dishes at the same meal.

fil.description: Pork na double-fried hanggang shatteringly crisp, tapos hinalo sa ketchup-and-vinegar sauce na sini-simmer nang mabagal with star anise hanggang glossy — ang dish na nagpapasaya kahit sa mga ayaw kumain ng gulay.
ingredients: pork shoulder o tenderloin, hiwain into bite-sized chunks
garlic powder, plus 1/4 tsp onion powder
cornstarch, itabi ang 1 tsp para sa sauce-thickening slurry
green bell pepper, hiwain into 3cm squares
steps: I-toss ang pork sa marinade (tubig, toyo, sesame oil, garlic powder at onion powder) hanggang walang natitirang liquid; itabi for 30 minutes.

Gawin ang sauce base: painitin ang oil sa maliit na saucepan, idagdag ang luya at star anise, at lutuin hanggang mabango at lightly caramelized, about 1 minute. Idagdag ang ketchup at haluin hanggang bahagyang dumilim, about 2 minutes.

Idagdag ang vinegar, asukal at itinabing pineapple juice. I-simmer nang hindi natatakpan sa low heat, haluin paminsan-minsan, for about 30 minutes hanggang glossy ang sauce at ma-coat ang likod ng kutsara.
Painitin ang deep-frying oil to 175°C (350°F). I-dredge ang marinated pork sa flour-cornstarch mixture, isawsaw sa binitin na itlog, tapos i-dredge ulit.
Iprito ang pork in batches for 2-3 minutes hanggang golden at luto na; i-drain. Bago ihain, i-re-fry ulit ang lahat ng pork for 30-60 seconds para maging extra crisp.
I-stir-fry ang bell pepper at sibuyas sa splash ng oil sa high heat for 30 seconds.
Ibuhos ang sweet and sour sauce at ang pineapple chunks; i-simmer para lumapot, dagdagan ng kaunting itinabing cornstarch mixture na hinaluan ng tubig kung kailangan pang lumapot.
Idagdag ang crispy pork, i-toss agad para ma-coat na hindi tumatagal sa sauce, at ihain agad para manatiling crunchy.
tips: I-prito nang dalawang beses ang pork: una para maluto, tapos fast second fry bago i-sauce — iyon ang gumagawa nito na crunchy pa rin sa ilalim ng sauce instead of soggy.
I-toss lang ang pinaprito na pork sa sauce bago ihain; nawawalan ng crunch agad ang pork kung matagal sa sauce.
fil.nutritionNote: Ito ang pinakamayaman na dish sa rotation, deep-fried batter plus sugar-and-ketchup sauce, kaya ituring itong occasional treat, ihain ng mas maliit na portions kasama ng maraming plain rice at green vegetable, at iwasan ang ibang fried o sweet na dishes sa parehong meal.

recipes.title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
recipes.localTitle: Fan Qie Chao Dan (番茄炒蛋)
recipes.description: Ripe tomatoes stir-fried down into a sweet-savory sauce and folded through soft scrambled eggs — the dish every Chinese kid grows up eating over rice, ready faster than delivery.
steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and finely chop the scallions.
Crack the eggs into a bowl with half the salt, the white pepper, sesame oil and Shaoxing wine; beat well for a minute.
Heat a wok over medium heat until smoking, add half the oil, and pour in the eggs. Scramble into large soft curds and remove before fully set; set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok, turn the heat to high, and stir-fry the tomatoes and scallions for 1 minute until they just start to release their juice.
Add the sugar, remaining salt and water; stir to combine.
Return the eggs to the wok, cover, and cook 1-2 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down into a light sauce.
Uncover and stir-fry over high heat until the sauce reaches a loose, saucy consistency that coats rice well.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.
tips: Scramble the eggs until just barely set and pull them early — they finish cooking when folded back in, and overcooked eggs turn rubbery.
Use the ripest, reddest tomatoes you can find; the whole sauce is built from their juice plus a little sugar to round out the acidity.
recipes.nutritionNote: A genuinely balanced weeknight plate with real vegetable content from the tomatoes plus protein from the eggs — just watch the added sugar and oil if serving very small portions.

fil.description: Hinog na kamatis na sini-stir-fry hanggang maging sweet-savory sauce at hinalo sa soft scrambled eggs — ang dish na kinakain ng bawat batang Chinese habang lumalaki over rice, mas mabilis pa kaysa delivery.
steps: Hiwain ang kamatis into wedges at tadtarin nang pino ang scallions.
Basagin ang itlog sa bowl kasama ang half ng asin, white pepper, sesame oil at Shaoxing wine; i-beat nang mabuti for a minute.
Painitin ang wok sa medium heat hanggang umuusok, idagdag ang half ng oil, at ibuhos ang itlog. I-scramble into large soft curds at alisin before fully set; itabi.
Idagdag ang natitirang oil sa wok, taasan ang heat to high, at i-stir-fry ang kamatis at scallions for 1 minute hanggang magsimulang lumabas ang katas nito.
Idagdag ang asukal, natitirang asin at tubig; haluin.
Ibalik ang itlog sa wok, takpan, at lutuin for 1-2 minutes hanggang madurog ang kamatis into light sauce.
Alisin ang takip at i-stir-fry sa high heat hanggang umabot sa loose at saucy consistency na nag-coat nang maayos sa kanin.
Ihain agad over steamed rice.
tips: I-scramble ang itlog hanggang just barely set at alisin agad — matatapos ang pagluluto nila kapag inihalo ulit, at nagiging rubbery ang overcooked na itlog.
Gumamit ng pinakahinog at pinakapulang kamatis — ang buong sauce ay galing sa katas nila plus kaunting asukal para i-balance ang acidity.
fil.nutritionNote: Genuinely balanced na weeknight plate na may real vegetable content mula sa kamatis plus protein mula sa itlog — bantayan lang ang added sugar at oil kung maliliit na portions ang ihahain.

recipes.title: Twice-Cooked Pork
recipes.description: Pork belly is boiled whole, sliced thin, then seared and stir-fried with doubanjiang, leeks and chillies until the edges crisp — Sichuan's classic use for a slab of pork belly.

ingredients.item: leek, white and light green parts, sliced diagonally

steps: Place the pork belly in a pot with the ginger and enough cold water to cover; bring to a boil, then simmer 25 minutes until a chopstick pierces it easily.
Drain and cool the pork until firm enough to slice, then slice very thinly, about 3mm thick, against the grain.
Heat a dry wok over medium heat and sear the pork slices with no oil for 3-4 minutes until the fat renders and the edges curl and turn golden.
Push the pork to one side, add the oil and doubanjiang to the cleared space, and fry 30 seconds until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add the garlic, stir-fry 20 seconds, then toss everything together in the wok.
Add the chillies and leek, stir-fry over high heat for 1-2 minutes until the leek is just wilted but still bright green.
Splash in the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces and sugar; toss for 30 seconds to coat evenly, then serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Boil the pork whole and slice it only after it cools — this two-step cooking is what gives the dish its name and its texture.
Real Pixian doubanjiang gives the authentic malty heat; other chilli bean sauces taste flatter.
recipes.kidNote: This is genuinely spicy from the doubanjiang and green chillies. Cook the kids' portion before adding the chillies, use half the doubanjiang for their share, and finish it with just the soy sauces and sugar.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pork belly is rich in saturated fat, so keep portions modest and balance the plate with extra steamed greens or a cucumber salad.

fil.description: Buong pork belly ang nilulutong pakuluan, hiniwa nang manipis, tapos sinangag at ginisa kasama ng doubanjiang, leeks at sili hanggang crisp ang gilid — classic use ng Sichuan para sa isang slab ng pork belly.
ingredients: maanghang na doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste)
mahabang berdeng sili, hiniwa nang pahilis
leek, puti at light green na bahagi, hiniwa nang pahilis
steps: Ilagay ang pork belly sa pot kasama ang luya at sapat na malamig na tubig para matakpan; pakuluin, tapos i-simmer ng 25 minutes hanggang madaling tinutusok ng chopstick.
I-drain at palamigin ang pork hanggang matigas nang mahiwa, tapos hiwain nang napakanipis, mga 3mm ang kapal, laban sa grain.
Painitin ang tuyong wok sa medium heat at isangag ang mga hiwa ng pork nang walang mantika for 3-4 minutes hanggang lumabas ang taba at mag-golden ang gilid.
Itabi ang pork sa isang gilid, idagdag ang mantika at doubanjiang sa nabakanteng espasyo, tapos igisa ng 30 seconds hanggang pumula at umamoy masarap ang mantika.
Idagdag ang bawang, igisa ng 20 seconds, tapos ihalo ang lahat sa wok.
Idagdag ang sili at leek, igisa sa high heat for 1-2 minutes hanggang malanta lang ang leek pero bright green pa rin.
Buhusan ng Shaoxing wine, dalawang soy sauces at asukal; haluin ng 30 seconds para mabalutan nang pantay, tapos ihaing mainit na may kanin.
tips: Ipakulo muna ang pork nang buo at hiwain lang pagkatapos lumamig — itong two-step cooking ang nagbibigay ng pangalan at texture ng ulam.
Ang totoong Pixian doubanjiang ang nagbibigay ng authentic na malty heat; mas flat ang lasa ng ibang chili bean sauce.
fil.kidNote: Talagang maanghang ito dahil sa doubanjiang at berdeng sili. Lutuin muna ang portion ng mga bata bago ilagay ang sili, gamitin ang kalahati ng doubanjiang para sa kanila, tapos tapusin lang ng soy sauces at asukal.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa saturated fat ang pork belly, kaya panatilihing katamtaman ang serving at i-balance ang plato ng extra steamed greens o cucumber salad.

recipes.title: West Lake Beef Soup
recipes.localTitle: Xi Hu Niu Rou Geng (西湖牛肉羹)
recipes.description: Minced beef, silken tofu and ribbons of egg white are simmered in a light broth thickened just enough to turn velvety — a gentle Hangzhou soup that comes together in half an hour.

ingredients.item: soft tofu, cut into small cubes
yellow chives or scallion, cut into short lengths

steps: Mix the minced beef with cornstarch, water and light soy sauce and let it sit for 10 minutes to velvet.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil, drop in the beef in small clumps, and parboil for 20-30 seconds just until it changes color, then drain and set aside.
Bring the chicken broth to a gentle boil in a clean pot.
Stir the cornstarch slurry once more and pour it into the broth in a thin stream, stirring constantly, until the broth thickens to a light, velvety consistency.
Gently add the parboiled beef and tofu cubes to the thickened broth and let it return to a simmer.
Drizzle in the beaten egg whites in a thin stream while stirring slowly, so they set into soft ribbons.
Season with salt, white pepper and sesame oil, add the yellow chives, and simmer 1 more minute before serving hot.
tips: Parboiling the beef separately before it goes into the broth is what keeps the soup clear instead of cloudy.
Pour the egg whites in slowly while stirring gently — pouring fast or stirring hard breaks them into small flecks instead of silky ribbons.
recipes.nutritionNote: This is a light, easily digestible soup with lean protein from beef and tofu; use a low-sodium broth and adjust the added salt to taste to keep sodium in check.

fil.description: Minced na beef, silken tofu at hibla ng puti ng itlog ang niluluto sa magaan na sabaw na pinalapot lang hanggang maging velvety — mahinahong sabaw ng Hangzhou na tapos sa loob ng kalahating oras.
ingredients: soft tofu, hinawa sa maliliit na cubes
puti ng itlog, hinalo nang bahagya
yellow chives o scallion, hinawa sa maiikling piraso
steps: Haluin ang minced beef sa cornstarch, tubig at light soy sauce tapos hayaan itong itabi for 10 minutes para mag-velvet.
Ipakulo ang maliit na pot ng tubig, ilagay ang beef nang paisa-isang tumpok, at parboil for 20-30 seconds hanggang magpalit lang ng kulay, tapos i-drain at itabi.
Ipakulo nang mahinang mahina ang chicken broth sa malinis na pot.
Haluin ulit ang cornstarch slurry tapos ibuhos ito sa sabaw nang manipis, haluin nang tuloy-tuloy, hanggang lumapot ang sabaw sa magaan, velvety na consistency.
Dahan-dahang idagdag ang parboiled na beef at tofu cubes sa lumapot na sabaw at hayaang bumalik sa simmer.
Patakan ang hinalong puti ng itlog nang manipis habang dahan-dahang hinahalo, para mag-set ito bilang malambot na hibla.
Timplahan ng asin, white pepper at sesame oil, idagdag ang yellow chives, tapos i-simmer ng 1 minute more bago ihaing mainit.
tips: Ang hiwalay na pag-parboil sa beef bago isama sa sabaw ang nagpapanatili nitong malinaw imbes na malabo.
Ibuhos ang puti ng itlog nang dahan-dahan habang gently hinahalo — ang mabilis na pagbuhos o malakas na paghalo ay nagsisira nito papunta sa maliliit na piraso imbes na silky na hibla.
fil.nutritionNote: Magaan at madaling matunaw ang sabaw na ito na may lean protein mula sa beef at tofu; gumamit ng low-sodium broth at i-adjust ang idinagdag na asin ayon sa panlasa para makontrol ang sodium.

recipes.title: Winter Melon and Pork Rib Soup
recipes.localTitle: Dong Gua Pai Gu Tang (冬瓜排骨汤)
recipes.description: Pork ribs are simmered slow with ginger until the broth turns clean and savory, then winter melon is added at the end to soften into a light, translucent, comforting soup.

ingredients.item: winter melon, peeled and cut into chunks
scallion or cilantro, chopped, for garnish

steps: Soak the pork ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out blood, then drain.
Blanch the ribs in a pot of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, skimming off any scum, then rinse the ribs under cold water.
Return the ribs to a clean pot with the ginger and the 2 litres of water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 90 minutes, checking occasionally, until the ribs are very tender and the broth tastes rich.
Add the winter melon chunks and salt, and simmer uncovered for a further 15 minutes until the melon turns translucent.
Season with white pepper and adjust salt to taste.
Ladle into bowls, scatter with scallion or cilantro, and serve hot with rice or on its own.
tips: Blanching the ribs first is what keeps the final broth clear instead of cloudy.
Leave a thin strip of the dark green skin on some winter melon pieces so they hold their shape through the long simmer.
recipes.nutritionNote: This is a light, low-fat broth once the ribs are skimmed of scum; it is naturally low in sodium if you go easy on the added salt, and it makes a gentle, hydrating starter alongside a vegetable stir-fry.

fil.description: Nilulutong dahan-dahan ang pork ribs kasama ng luya hanggang malinis at masarap ang sabaw, tapos idadagdag ang winter melon sa huli para lumambot nang translucent — magaan, nakakaaliw na sabaw.
ingredients: pork ribs, hinawa sa 3-4cm na piraso
winter melon, balat na at hinawa
steps: Ibabad ang pork ribs sa malamig na tubig for 30 minutes para mahugot ang dugo, tapos i-drain.
I-blanch ang ribs sa kumukulong tubig for 1-2 minutes, alisin ang bulang lumulutang, tapos banlawan sa malamig na tubig.
Ibalik ang ribs sa malinis na pot kasama ang luya at ang 2 litro ng tubig, pakuluin, tapos hinaan papunta sa mahinang simmer.
Takpan at i-simmer for 90 minutes, tingnan paminsan-minsan, hanggang napakalambot na ng ribs at masarap na ang sabaw.
Idagdag ang winter melon chunks at asin, tapos i-simmer nang hindi natatakpan for another 15 minutes hanggang maging translucent ang melon.
Timplahan ng white pepper at i-adjust ang asin ayon sa panlasa.
Isalin sa mga bowl, budburan ng scallion o cilantro, tapos ihaing mainit na may kanin o mag-isa.
tips: Ang pag-blanch muna sa ribs ang nagpapanatiling malinaw imbes na malabo ang sabaw sa huli.
Iwanan ang manipis na strip ng madilim na berdeng balat sa ilang piraso ng winter melon para manatili ang hugis nito kahit matagal ang simmer.
fil.nutritionNote: Magaan at mababa sa taba ang sabaw na ito kapag naalis na ang bula sa ribs; naturally mababa sa sodium kung bahagya lang ang asin na ilalagay, at magandang gentle, hydrating na starter kasama ng ginisang gulay.

recipes.title: Wonton Noodle Soup
recipes.description: Hong Kong-style thin egg noodles in a clear, savoury broth with plump pork-and-shrimp wontons — light, bouncy and the classic late-night snack of Cantonese noodle shops.
steps: Combine the pork, shrimp, sesame oil, soy sauce, white pepper and cornstarch in a bowl and mix briskly in one direction until slightly sticky, about 2 minutes.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the centre of each wrapper, wet the edges, fold into a triangle and press the corners together to seal.
Bring the chicken broth to a simmer and season with salt; keep it hot but not boiling.
Bring a separate pot of water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, 1-2 minutes, then drain and divide among bowls.
In the same pot, boil the wontons for 4-5 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles, top with the wontons, and garnish with scallions and a drizzle of sesame oil.
tips: A food processor pulses the pork-shrimp filling to a bouncy paste in under a minute if you don't want to mix by hand.
recipes.kidNote: No spice to adjust; cut the wontons in half for younger kids so they're easier to eat with a spoon.
recipes.nutritionNote: Most of the sodium here comes from the broth and the soy-seasoned filling, so taste before adding extra salt, and boiling rather than frying keeps the dish light on fat.

fil.description: Manipis na egg noodles ng Hong Kong sa malinaw, masarap na sabaw na may malamlam na pork-and-shrimp wontons — magaan, bouncy at ang classic late-night snack sa mga Cantonese noodle shop.
steps: Haluin ang pork, hipon, sesame oil, soy sauce, white pepper at cornstarch sa isang bowl at haluin nang mabilis sa iisang direksyon hanggang medyo malagkit, mga 2 minutes.
Maglagay ng kaunting sahog sa gitna ng bawat wrapper, basain ang gilid, i-fold papunta sa triangle at pisilin ang mga sulok para magsara.
Ipakulo ang chicken broth nang mahina at timplahan ng asin; panatilihing mainit pero hindi kumukulo.
Ipakulo ang hiwalay na pot ng tubig at lutuin ang noodles hanggang maluto lang, 1-2 minutes, tapos i-drain at hatiin sa mga bowl.
Sa parehong pot, ipakulo ang wontons for 4-5 minutes hanggang lumutang at maluto na ang sahog.
Ibuhos ang mainit na sabaw sa ibabaw ng noodles, patungan ng wontons, at budburan ng scallions at kaunting sesame oil.
tips: Isang minuto lang ng food processor at magiging bouncy paste na ang pork-shrimp filling kung ayaw mo nang gawin sa kamay.
fil.kidNote: Walang anghang na i-a-adjust; hatiin sa kalahati ang wontons para sa mas batang bata para mas madaling kainin gamit ang kutsara.
fil.nutritionNote: Karamihan ng sodium dito ay galing sa sabaw at soy-seasoned na filling, kaya tikman muna bago lagyan pa ng asin; boiling instead of frying ang nagpapanatiling magaan ang taba ng ulam.

recipes.title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
recipes.description: Day-old rice fried hot and fast with shrimp, char siu, egg, carrot and peas until every grain separates — Yangzhou's answer to leftovers and the fried rice every other version gets compared to.

ingredients.note: cook a day ahead and cool completely

ingredients.item: shrimp, peeled, deveined and halved lengthwise
scallion, white and green parts separated, chopped

steps: Cook the rice with slightly less water than usual so the grains stay firm; spread out and cool completely, ideally a day ahead — wet, fresh rice turns fried rice mushy.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch the carrot and peas for 30-40 seconds, then add the shrimp and cook until just pink, about 2 more minutes. Drain and set aside.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of the salt.
Heat a wok over high heat for a minute, add 1 tablespoon of oil until rippling, then pour in the eggs. Let them set for 10-15 seconds, then add the cold rice directly on top.
Break up the rice clumps and stir-fry for 2.5-3 minutes over high heat until each grain separates and you hear a light crackle.
Lower the heat, add half the salt and the soy sauce, and toss to coat evenly.
Push the rice to the sides of the wok, add the char siu to the center to warm through, then mix it in along with the blanched vegetables, shrimp and scallion whites.
Raise the heat to high, drizzle in the remaining oil for shine, toss everything together, and finish with the scallion greens.
tips: Cold, dry, day-old rice is non-negotiable — fresh rice is too wet and clumps instead of frying into separate grains.
Get the wok smoking hot before the eggs go in; a lukewarm wok is the most common reason home fried rice turns out steamed instead of stir-fried.
recipes.nutritionNote: A complete one-bowl meal with protein from shrimp, egg and char siu already built in, but char siu and soy sauce both bring sodium, so skip extra salt at the table and add a side of blanched vegetables if serving as a whole dinner.

fil.description: Kanin na day-old, sini-stir-fry hot and fast with hipon, char siu, itlog, carrot at gisantes hanggang maghiwalay ang bawat butil — ito ang sagot ng Yangzhou sa leftovers at ang fried rice na pinagkukumparahan ng lahat ng version.
ingredients: tubig, para sa pagluluto ng kanin
hipon, balatan, alisan ng ugat at hiwain into half lengthwise
scallion, white at green parts hiwalayin, tadtarin
steps: Lutuin ang kanin gamit ng kaunti lang na tubig kaysa usual para manatiling matigas ang butil; i-spread out at palamigin nang husto, ideally isang araw before — nagiging mushy ang fried rice kapag basa at bagong-luto ang kanin.
Pakuluan ang tubig. I-blanch ang carrot at peas for 30-40 seconds, tapos idagdag ang hipon at lutuin hanggang just pink, about 2 more minutes. I-drain at itabi.
I-beat ang itlog with pinch ng asin.
Painitin ang wok sa high heat for a minute, idagdag ang 1 tbsp oil hanggang rippling, tapos ibuhos ang itlog. Hayaang mag-set for 10-15 seconds, tapos idagdag ang malamig na kanin diretso sa ibabaw.
Durugin ang mga clumps ng kanin at i-stir-fry for 2.5-3 minutes sa high heat hanggang maghiwalay ang bawat butil at maririnig ang light crackle.
Ibaba ang heat, idagdag ang half ng asin at ang soy sauce, at i-toss para maging pantay ang coating.
Itabi ang kanin sa gilid ng wok, idagdag ang char siu sa gitna para mainitan, tapos ihalo kasama ang blanched vegetables, hipon at scallion whites.
Taasan ang heat to high, i-drizzle ang natitirang oil para sa shine, i-toss ang lahat nang sabay, at i-finish ng scallion greens.
tips: Non-negotiable ang malamig at tuyong day-old na kanin — masyadong basa ang bagong-luto na kanin at nagkukulumpon instead na maghiwalay ang mga butil sa pagpi-fry.
Siguraduhing umuusok na ang wok before ilagay ang itlog; ang pangkaraniwang dahilan kung bakit nagiging steamed instead of stir-fried ang fried rice sa bahay ay lukewarm na wok.
fil.nutritionNote: Complete one-bowl meal ito na may protein na mula sa hipon, itlog at char siu — pero maalat ang char siu at soy sauce, kaya skip na lang ang extra salt sa table at magdagdag ng blanched vegetables kung buong dinner ang ihahain.

recipes.title: Zhajiangmian
recipes.description: Beijing's everyday noodle dish: thick wheat noodles tossed with a savoury-sweet ground pork and fermented bean paste sauce, topped with crisp raw cucumber matchsticks.

ingredients.note: or hoisin sauce mixed with a little dark soy

steps: Mix the sweet bean paste and yellow bean paste with the water until smooth and pourable.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and cook the ginger until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the ground pork and break it up, browning it for 3-4 minutes until no longer pink.
Splash in the Shaoxing wine, then pour in the diluted bean paste and simmer, stirring often, for 10 minutes until glossy and thickened.
Stir in the diced onion and cook 3-5 minutes more until softened.
Boil the noodles until just cooked, 2-3 minutes for fresh noodles, then drain and divide among bowls.
Top each bowl with the pork sauce and a handful of cucumber matchsticks, then toss together at the table before eating.
tips: Keep the sauce on the thick side — it should coat the noodles, not pool at the bottom of the bowl.
recipes.kidNote: No adjustment needed; the sauce is savoury-sweet, not spicy, and kids usually like mixing it themselves.
recipes.nutritionNote: The fermented bean paste and pork are salty and fatty; go light on any extra soy sauce at the table and let the raw cucumber do the balancing.

fil.description: Everyday noodle dish ng Beijing: makapal na wheat noodles na hinalo sa savoury-sweet ground pork at fermented bean paste sauce, may toppings na crisp raw cucumber matchsticks.
steps: Haluin ang sweet bean paste at yellow bean paste sa tubig hanggang maging smooth at pwedeng ibuhos.
Painitin ang mantika sa wok sa medium heat at igisa ang luya hanggang umamoy masarap, mga 30 seconds.
Idagdag ang ground pork at durugin habang niluluto, i-brown for 3-4 minutes hanggang wala nang pink.
Buhusan ng Shaoxing wine, tapos ibuhos ang tinunaw na bean paste at i-simmer, haluin madalas, for 10 minutes hanggang glossy at lumapot.
Idagdag ang dinaing na onion at lutuin ng 3-5 minutes more hanggang lumambot.
Ipakulo ang noodles hanggang maluto lang, 2-3 minutes para sa fresh noodles, tapos i-drain at hatiin sa mga bowl.
Patungan ang bawat bowl ng pork sauce at kaunting cucumber matchsticks, tapos haluin sa table bago kainin.
tips: Panatilihing makapal ang sauce — dapat sumasama ito sa noodles, hindi natitira lang sa ilalim ng bowl.
fil.kidNote: Walang kailangang i-adjust; savoury-sweet lang ang sauce, hindi maanghang, at gustong-gusto ng mga bata na sila mismo ang maghalo nito.
fil.nutritionNote: Maalat at mamantika ang fermented bean paste at pork, kaya bawasan ang extra soy sauce sa table at hayaan ang raw cucumber na mag-balance.

recipes.title: Adobong Kangkong
recipes.description: Water spinach braised adobo-style with pork belly in vinegar and soy sauce — a quick, budget-friendly way to get greens onto the table alongside grilled or fried fish.

ingredients.item: kangkong (water spinach), trimmed and cut into 3-inch lengths
pork belly, cut into thin strips

steps: Wash the kangkong, keeping the sturdier stalks separate from the leaves.
Heat oil in a wide skillet; sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
Add vinegar and boil uncovered without stirring for 2-3 minutes.
Add soy sauce and water; bring to a boil.
Lower heat, cover, and simmer 8-10 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce is reduced.
Raise the heat to high, add the kangkong stalks and cook 1-2 minutes.
Add the kangkong leaves and cook, stirring, about 1 minute until just wilted.
Season with salt and pepper; serve hot with rice.
tips: Add the stalks before the leaves since they need a little longer to soften.
Don't overcook the kangkong — pull it off the heat as soon as the leaves wilt, since residual heat keeps cooking it.
recipes.kidNote: The vinegar makes this a fairly sour dish — serve the sauce on the side for picky kids and let them spoon on only as much as they like, rather than starting with a very saucy bowl.
recipes.nutritionNote: Kangkong is a good source of iron and fibre; the pork belly adds richness, so use a smaller amount or swap in a leaner cut if serving this often.

fil.description: Kangkong na niluto adobo-style with pork belly sa suka at toyo — mabilis, budget-friendly na paraan para makakuha ng gulay sa mesa kasabay ng inihaw o pritong isda.
ingredients: kangkong, trimmed at hiwain into 3-inch lengths
pork belly, hiniwa into thin strips
steps: Hugasan ang kangkong, ihiwalay ang matigas na tangkay sa mga dahon.
Painitin ang mantika sa malapad na skillet; igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang lumambot.
Idagdag ang baboy at lutuin hanggang bahagyang mag-brown.
Idagdag ang suka at pakuluin nang hindi tinatakpan at hindi hinahalo for 2-3 minutes.
Idagdag ang toyo at tubig; pakuluin.
Hinaan ang apoy, takpan, at i-simmer for 8-10 minutes hanggang lumambot ang baboy at reduced na ang sabaw.
Lakasan ang apoy, ilagay ang tangkay ng kangkong at lutuin for 1-2 minutes.
Idagdag ang mga dahon ng kangkong at lutuin, haluin, for about 1 minute hanggang malanta lang.
Timplahan ng asin at paminta; ihain mainit with rice.
tips: Ilagay ang tangkay bago ang mga dahon dahil mas matagal itong lumambot.
Huwag masyadong lutuin ang kangkong — alisin sa apoy as soon as malanta ang mga dahon, dahil tumutuloy pa ang pagkaluto dahil sa residual heat.
fil.kidNote: Medyo maasim ang dish na ito dahil sa suka — ihain ang sabaw nang hiwalay para sa mapili kumain na bata at hayaan silang mag-spoon ng kaunti lang, imbes na simulan sa very saucy na bowl.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang source ng iron at fiber ang kangkong; nagdadagdag ng richness ang pork belly, kaya gumamit ng mas kaunti o palitan ng leaner cut kung madalas ihahain ito.

recipes.title: Arroz Caldo
recipes.description: A thick, ginger-scented rice porridge with shredded chicken, topped with crispy garlic, egg and scallions — the standard Filipino sick-day and rainy-morning breakfast.

ingredients.note: or a whole chicken cut into pieces
mix half-and-half with regular rice for a looser porridge

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat; sauté the onion, ginger and garlic until softened and fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring, until lightly browned on the outside.
Pour in the fish sauce and cook 1-2 minutes to let the chicken absorb the flavour.
Stir in the rice and cook 1-2 minutes, toasting it lightly in the aromatics.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam; add the bouillon cubes and stir to dissolve.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer 30-35 minutes, stirring every few minutes so the rice doesn't stick, until the porridge thickens and the chicken is cooked through.
Shred or pull the chicken into bite-sized pieces if you like, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls and top with hard-boiled egg, fried garlic and green onions; serve with calamansi and extra fish sauce on the side.
tips: Stir every few minutes once the rice goes in — glutinous rice scorches on the bottom easily.
Fry the garlic bits separately and low and slow; they go from golden to burnt in seconds.
Leftover porridge thickens a lot in the fridge — loosen with a splash of hot water or stock when reheating.
recipes.nutritionNote: A soft, easy-to-digest rice porridge that's fairly plain on its own; the egg and shredded chicken supply protein, so add a side of sautéed vegetables since the dish itself offers little fibre.

fil.description: Makapal, maluyang rice porridge na may shredded chicken, tinopping ng crispy garlic, itlog at scallions — ang standard Filipino sick-day at rainy-morning breakfast.
ingredients: hita at paa ng manok, bone-in
hard-boiled na itlog, hiwain in half
steps: Painitin ang oil sa heavy pot sa medium heat; igisa ang sibuyas, luya at bawang hanggang lumambot at mabango.
Idagdag ang manok at lutuin, haluin, hanggang lightly browned sa labas.
Ibuhos ang patis at lutuin for 1-2 minutes para maabsorb ng manok ang lasa.
Ihalo ang bigas at lutuin for 1-2 minutes, i-toast nang bahagya sa mga aromatics.
Ibuhos ang tubig, pakuluin, at alisin ang foam na lumulutang; idagdag ang bouillon cubes at haluin hanggang matunaw.
Hinaan ang apoy, takpan, at i-simmer for 30-35 minutes, haluin every few minutes para hindi dumikit ang bigas, hanggang lumapot ang lugaw at luto na ang manok.
I-shred o hilahin ang manok into bite-sized pieces kung gusto mo, tapos timplahan ng asin at paminta to taste.
Isalin sa bowl at topping ng hard-boiled egg, fried garlic at green onions; ihain with calamansi at extra patis sa tabi.
tips: Haluin every few minutes once nasa loob na ang bigas — mabilis mag-scorch ang malagkit sa ilalim.
I-fry ang garlic bits separately at low and slow; mabilis lang siyang mag-golden hanggang sunog.
Lumalapot nang husto ang natirang lugaw sa ref — lagyan ng konting mainit na tubig o stock kapag ni-reheat.
fil.nutritionNote: Malambot, madaling matunaw na rice porridge na medyo plain lang mag-isa; ang itlog at shredded chicken ang nagbibigay ng protein, kaya dagdagan ng sautéed vegetables dahil kaunti lang ang fibre ng dish mismo.

recipes.title: Banana Cue
recipes.description: Whole saba bananas deep-fried and rolled in melting brown sugar until they're glazed and sticky, then skewered on bamboo sticks — a three-ingredient snack sold from carts every late afternoon.

ingredients.note: ripe but firm, with yellow skin and a few black spots
helps the sugar melt into an even syrup rather than clumping
optional, stirred into the sugar to cut the sweetness slightly

steps: Heat the oil in a wok or deep pan over medium heat to about 350°F (180°C).
Add the peeled bananas in batches, without crowding the pan, and fry 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and tender.
Sprinkle in half the brown sugar with a splash of the water and a pinch of salt, and keep tossing the bananas gently so they get evenly coated as the sugar melts and caramelizes.
