recipes.nutritionNote: Rich in fat from the nuts, seeds and lard used to build the sauce; balance the plate with plain rice and a simple salad rather than more fried sides.

fil.description: Manok na ni-simmer sa malalim na toasted-chilli at Mexican-chocolate sauce galing Puebla — savory muna ang lasa, may bahagyang tamis lang once matapos maluto.
ingredients: bone-in na hita at paa ng manok
white onion, hiwain nang four parts
ancho chillies, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
guajillo chillies, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
pasilla chillies, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
sesame seeds, plus extra for garnish
steps: Pagsamahin ang manok, water, onion at bawang sa large pot, ipakulo, tapos hinaan ang apoy at i-simmer for 35 minutes hanggang maluto lang ang manok. Alisin ang manok at salain ang broth; itabi muna pareho.

Punasan ang dried chillies tapos i-toast nang paisa-isa sa dry skillet, ipatag gamit ang spatula, hanggang mabango at maging tobacco-brown ang flesh, mga 20 seconds per side — huwag hayaang mag-itim kundi papait ang sauce. Ibabad ang toasted chillies sa 2 cups ng hot broth.
Sa parehong skillet may konting lard, iprito ang raisins hanggang mag-plump, ang almonds hanggang golden, at ang sesame seeds hanggang pumutok; i-drain ang bawat isa sa plato.
Iprito ang tortilla at plantain slices sa parehong skillet hanggang mag-brown, tapos idagdag sa parehong plato kasama ang roasted tomatoes.
In batches, i-blend ang nabababad na chillies kasama ang broth nila, ang mga fried ingredients, cinnamon, at 1 cup fresh broth hanggang completely smooth; salain kung may natitirang grit.
Painitin ang natitirang lard sa wide pot, ibuhos ang blended sauce, tapos iprito ito, haluin nang tuloy-tuloy, hanggang dumilim at lumapot, mga 10 minutes.

Ihalo ang chocolate at sapat na broth para maging gravy-like ang consistency, tapos i-simmer nang walang takip for 25–30 minutes, haluin madalas para hindi masunog, hanggang lumitaw ang maliliit na oil sa ibabaw.
Timplahan ng asin, ilagay ang lutong manok, tapos i-simmer 10 minutes more hanggang mainit na ulit. Ihain sa ibabaw ng manok with sprinkle of sesame seeds, plain white rice, at warm tortillas.
tips: Talagang weekend project ito — 3 separately toasted components at two-stage blend — pero maganda mag-freeze ang sauce for 3 months, kaya sulit i-double.
I-toast ang chillies in small batches; kapag napuno ng matalim na usok ang kusina, nasunog na ang mga ito at mapapait kahit magkano pang chocolate ang idagdag mo.
fil.kidNote: Mild at rounded ang lasa ng tapos na mole, hindi maanghang; pwedeng kumain ng parehong plato ang mga bata kasama ng adults. Kung ayaw talaga nila ng chilli, isandok ang portion nila bago mo pa lagyan ng dagdag na asin.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa fat mula sa nuts, seeds, at lard na ginamit sa sauce; i-balance ang plato with plain rice at simpleng salad imbes na dagdag na fried sides.

recipes.title: Molletes
recipes.description: Split bread rolls spread with refried beans and melted cheese, broiled until bubbling — Mexico's everyday cafeteria breakfast or afternoon snack.

ingredients.item: bolillo rolls or other crusty white rolls
ingredients.note: pandesal or a small split baguette are good Manila substitutes

steps: Preheat the broiler and cut the rolls in half lengthwise.
Scoop out a little of the soft crumb from the centre of each half to make room for the filling.
Spread the cut sides with butter and broil for 3-4 minutes until lightly golden.
Remove from the broiler and spread each half generously with warm refried beans.
Top with the shredded cheese and return to the broiler for 3-5 minutes until melted and bubbling.
Top with pico de gallo and serve with avocado slices on the side.
tips: Warm the beans before spreading so the broiler only needs to melt the cheese, not heat the whole thing through.
Watch the broiler closely in the last minute — cheese can go from melted to burnt fast.
recipes.nutritionNote: A balanced breakfast from the beans' fibre and protein and the bread's carbohydrates; the avocado adds healthy fat in place of extra cheese.

fil.description: Hinating bread rolls na pinahiran ng refried beans at natunaw na cheese, ni-broil hanggang bubbling — everyday cafeteria breakfast o afternoon snack sa Mexico.
ingredients: bolillo rolls o iba pang crusty white rolls
steps: I-preheat ang broiler tapos hiwain ang rolls in half lengthwise.
Kunin nang kaunti ang soft crumb sa gitna ng bawat half para may lagyan ng filling.
Pahiran ng butter ang cut sides tapos i-broil for 3-4 minutes hanggang medyo golden.
Alisin sa broiler tapos pahiran nang generous ang bawat half ng warm refried beans.
Lagyan ng shredded cheese tapos ibalik sa broiler for 3-5 minutes hanggang matunaw at bubbling na.
Lagyan ng pico de gallo tapos ihain with avocado slices sa gilid.
tips: I-warm muna ang beans bago pahiran para ang broiler na lang ang mag-melt ng cheese, hindi na kailangang painitin lahat.
Bantayan nang mabuti ang broiler sa last minute — mabilis lang magbago ang cheese from melted to burnt.
fil.nutritionNote: Balanced na breakfast mula sa fibre at protein ng beans at carbohydrates ng bread; nagdadagdag ang avocado ng healthy fat imbes na extra cheese.

recipes.title: Mushroom Quesadillas
recipes.description: Corn tortillas griddled with melted Oaxaca cheese and mushrooms sauteed with epazote and chile, a Mexico City street-stall staple that also makes a fast, meatless weeknight dinner.

ingredients.note: wild mushrooms are traditional in central Mexico; button or cremini are the easiest reliable substitute
deseed for a milder filling, or omit entirely
hard to find in Manila, order dried epazote online, or substitute a little chopped cilantro plus a pinch of dried oregano
mozzarella is the closest easy substitute

steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, chile and garlic, stir well, and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms release their liquid and it mostly evaporates, 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the epazote and salt in the last minute of cooking, then remove from heat.
Warm the corn tortillas on a dry griddle or comal until pliable, about 20 seconds per side.
Place a tortilla on the griddle, scatter cheese over half, top with a spoonful of the mushroom filling, and fold the tortilla over.
Press gently and cook 1-2 minutes per side until the tortilla is lightly toasted and the cheese has melted through.
Serve immediately with salsa on the side.
tips: Let the mushrooms fully release and cook off their own liquid before folding the quesadilla, or the tortilla will turn soggy.
Corn tortillas tear more easily than flour; warm them first so they fold without cracking.
recipes.nutritionNote: A meatless, fiber-rich option; the cheese provides protein and calcium, but keep portions moderate to avoid excess saturated fat if serving often.

source.name: Mexico in My Kitchen (sauteed mushroom filling), assembly per La Cocina de Leslie's Quesadillas de Hongos

fil.description: Corn tortillas na iginriddle with melted Oaxaca cheese at mushrooms na ginisa with epazote at chile, isang Mexico City street-stall staple na pwede ring maging fast, meatless weeknight dinner.
steps: Painitin ang oil sa skillet sa medium heat tapos lutuin ang onion hanggang maging translucent, mga 3 minutes.
Idagdag ang mushrooms, chile at garlic, haluin nang mabuti, tapos lutuin nang bukas, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang lumabas ang liquid ng mushrooms at halos ma-evaporate, 6-8 minutes.
Ihalo ang epazote at asin sa huling minuto ng pagluluto, tapos alisin sa apoy.
Painitin ang corn tortillas sa dry griddle o comal hanggang maging pliable, mga 20 seconds per side.
Ilagay ang tortilla sa griddle, budburan ng cheese sa kalahati, lagyan ng isang kutsara ng mushroom filling, tapos tiklupin ang tortilla.
Pindutin nang dahan-dahan tapos lutuin for 1-2 minutes per side hanggang lightly toasted ang tortilla at natunaw nang husto ang cheese.
Ihaing agad with salsa sa tabi.
tips: Hayaang lumabas nang husto at ma-evaporate ang liquid ng mushrooms bago tiklupin ang quesadilla, kung hindi mag-soggy ang tortilla.
Mas madaling mapunit ang corn tortillas kumpara sa flour; painitin muna para hindi mabasag kapag tiniklop.
fil.nutritionNote: Meatless, fiber-rich na option; nagbibigay ng protein at calcium ang cheese, pero konti lang ang portions para iwas sa excess saturated fat kung madalas ihahain.

recipes.title: Nopales con Huevo
recipes.description: Scrambled eggs cooked with tender cactus paddles, onion and garlic — a everyday Mexican breakfast that's earthy, a little tangy, and ready before the coffee finishes brewing.

ingredients.item: nopales (cactus paddles), cleaned, diced, and boiled until tender
ingredients.note: fresh nopales are rare here; jarred nopalitos (sold in some Latin/import grocers) are a fair swap — rinse well to cut the brine before using
kesong puti works well as a mild local substitute

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the cooked nopales and cook 3 more minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the beaten eggs and cook, stirring gently every 10 seconds, until light, fluffy and just set.
Season with salt and pepper and remove from heat immediately so the eggs don't overcook.
Serve hot, topped with crumbled cheese, with warm tortillas alongside.
tips: Stir gently and pull the pan off the heat a beat early — the eggs keep cooking in residual heat and go rubbery fast if left in the pan too long.
If using jarred nopalitos, pat them very dry after rinsing so the eggs don't turn watery.
recipes.nutritionNote: A high-protein, fibre-rich breakfast from the nopales; pair with beans and tortillas for a fuller, more balanced meal.

fil.description: Scrambled eggs na niluto with malambot na cactus paddles, onion, at bawang — everyday Mexican breakfast na earthy, bahagyang maasim, at tapos pa bago matapos mag-brew ang kape.
ingredients: nopales (cactus paddles), nalinis, dinice, at pinakuluan hanggang lumambot
durog na queso fresco, para sa serving
corn tortillas, pinainit, para sa serving
steps: Painitin ang oil sa large skillet sa medium-high heat.
Idagdag ang onion at bawang tapos lutuin, haluin, for 3 minutes hanggang lumambot at translucent ang onion.
Idagdag ang lutong nopales tapos lutuin 3 more minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan.
Ibuhos ang hinalong itlog tapos lutuin, haluin nang dahan-dahan every 10 seconds, hanggang light, fluffy, at just set.
Timplahan ng asin at pepper tapos alisin agad sa heat para hindi ma-overcook ang itlog.
Ihain mainit, lagyan ng durog na cheese sa ibabaw, with warm tortillas sa tabi.
tips: Haluin nang dahan-dahan tapos alisin ang pan sa heat nang mas maaga — patuloy pa ring niluluto ng residual heat ang itlog at mabilis maging rubbery kung matagal pa sa pan.
Kung jarred nopalitos ang ginamit, patuyuin nang mabuti after rinsing para hindi maging watery ang itlog.
fil.nutritionNote: High-protein at fibre-rich na breakfast mula sa nopales; i-pair with beans at tortillas para mas busog at balanced ang meal.

recipes.title: Pescado Zarandeado
recipes.description: A whole butterflied fish marinated in a smoky chile-citrus sauce and grilled over open flame until charred and flaky — Nayarit's classic beachside centerpiece.

ingredients.item: whole red snapper or similar white fish, butterflied and cleaned
ingredients.note: ask the wet market to butterfly it for you; maya-maya (mangrove red snapper) or lapu-lapu are good local substitutes

ingredients.item: dried guajillo chillies, stemmed and seeded
ingredients.note: order online from a Mexican-goods seller if unavailable locally

ingredients.item: dried ancho chillies, stemmed and seeded

ingredients.note: sold in Latin-goods sections or online; if unavailable, use 1 tsp paprika plus a pinch of turmeric for the color

steps: Toast the dried guajillo and ancho chillies in a dry skillet a few seconds per side until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the soaked chillies with the garlic, orange juice, lime juice, soy sauce, mayonnaise, mustard, achiote paste, oil and salt until completely smooth.
Lay the butterflied fish skin-side down and spread the marinade generously over the flesh, working it into the slashes. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.
Heat a charcoal grill to medium-high, or heat a large griddle indoors if grilling isn't possible.
Grill the fish flesh-side down first for 6–8 minutes until char marks form, then carefully flip to the skin side.
Continue grilling skin-side down for another 10–12 minutes, basting with any remaining marinade, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Transfer to a platter and serve whole with warm corn tortillas, sliced onion and lime wedges.
tips: A fish basket or two wire racks tied together makes flipping a whole butterflied fish over open coals far easier and keeps it from falling apart.
No grill? A very hot oven broiler with the fish on a sheet pan gets close, though you'll miss the smoke.
recipes.kidNote: The marinade has only mild warmth from the dried chillies with no fresh heat added, so it should suit the kids as-is; if they're sensitive, scrape a little of the marinade off their portion before serving.
recipes.nutritionNote: A lean, high-protein main; the mayonnaise in the marinade adds richness, so balance the plate with rice and a simple vegetable side rather than more sauce.

fil.description: Buong butterflied fish na ni-marinate sa smoky chile-citrus sauce tapos ni-grill sa open flame hanggang mag-char at maging flaky — classic beachside centerpiece ng Nayarit.
ingredients: buong red snapper o kahalintulad na white fish, na-butterfly at nalinis
guajillo chillies, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
ancho chillies, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
steps: I-toast ang guajillo at ancho chillies sa dry skillet for a few seconds per side hanggang mabango, tapos ibabad sa hot water for 15 minutes hanggang lumambot.
I-blend ang nababad na chillies with bawang, orange juice, lime juice, toyo, mayonnaise, mustard, achiote paste, oil, at asin hanggang completely smooth.
Ilatag ang butterflied fish skin-side down tapos ipahid nang generous ang marinade sa flesh, ipasok sa mga slashes. Takpan at i-refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.
Painitin ang charcoal grill to medium-high, o painitin ang large griddle indoors kung hindi puwedeng mag-grill.
I-grill ang fish flesh-side down muna for 6–8 minutes hanggang lumabas ang char marks, tapos i-flip nang maingat papunta sa skin side.
Ituloy ang pag-grill skin-side down for another 10–12 minutes, buhusan ng natitirang marinade, hanggang madaling mag-flake ang fish gamit ang fork.
Ilipat sa platter tapos ihain nang buo with warm corn tortillas, hiniwang onion, at lime wedges.
tips: Ang fish basket o two wire racks na naka-tali sa isa't isa ang mas nagpapadali sa pag-flip ng buong butterflied fish sa open coals at pumipigil dito na madurog.
Walang grill? Ang sobrang init na oven broiler na may fish sa sheet pan ay malapit na rin, kahit wala nang smoke.
fil.kidNote: Banayad lang ang init ng marinade mula sa dried chillies at walang added fresh heat, kaya dapat okay lang ito para sa mga bata as-is; kung sensitive sila, kayurin nang kaunti ang marinade sa portion nila bago ihain.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean at high-protein na main; nagdadagdag ng richness ang mayonnaise sa marinade, kaya i-balance ang plato with rice at simpleng vegetable side imbes na dagdag na sauce.

recipes.title: Picadillo
recipes.description: Ground beef simmered with potatoes, carrots and tomato until saucy, a homey everyday filling Mexican mothers make for tacos, stuffed peppers or simply spooned over rice.

ingredients.note: optional; more common in northern Mexican kitchens

steps: Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until no longer pink, 6-8 minutes, draining off excess fat if the mix looks greasy.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin and bay leaf, and cook 3-4 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the potatoes, carrot and broth, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes until the vegetables are just tender.
Stir in the peas, season with salt and pepper, and simmer uncovered 5 minutes more until the sauce thickens slightly and clings to the meat.
Remove the bay leaf and serve warm with warm corn tortillas or rice.
tips: Dice the potatoes small and uniform so they finish cooking in the same time as the beef.
Picadillo is even better the next day and freezes well for a quick future dinner.
recipes.nutritionNote: A balanced one-pot mix of protein, potato starch and vegetables; drain the grease after browning fattier beef to keep the dish lighter.

fil.description: Giniling na baka na ni-simmer sa patatas, carrot at kamatis hanggang saucy, isang homey everyday filling na madalas gawin ng mga Mexican mothers para sa tacos, stuffed peppers o basta ibuhos sa ibabaw ng rice.
ingredients: patatas, binalatan at dinice nang maliit
carrot, binalatan at dinice nang maliit
steps: Painitin ang oil sa wide skillet sa medium heat at lutuin ang onion hanggang lumambot, mga 3 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang at lutuin for 1 minute hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang giniling na baka, dikdikin gamit ang spoon, at lutuin hanggang hindi na pink, 6-8 minutes, i-drain ang sobrang taba kung maoily ang mixture.
Ihalo ang tomatoes, cumin at bay leaf, at lutuin for 3-4 minutes hanggang mag-breakdown ang tomatoes.
Idagdag ang patatas, carrot at broth, pakuluin, takpan, at lutuin for 15 minutes hanggang lumambot lang ang gulay.
Ihalo ang peas, timplahan ng asin at pepper, at i-simmer nang bukas for 5 minutes more hanggang lumapot nang kaunti ang sauce at dumikit sa karne.
Alisin ang bay leaf at ihain mainit with warm corn tortillas o rice.
tips: I-dice ang patatas nang maliit at pantay para maluto nang sabay sa beef.
Mas masarap pa ang picadillo the next day at freezer-friendly for a quick future dinner.
fil.nutritionNote: Balanced na one-pot mix ng protein, potato starch at gulay; i-drain ang grease after browning ng mataba na beef para mas light ang dish.

recipes.title: Pozole Verde
recipes.description: Guerrero-style hominy soup in a bright tomatillo, poblano and pumpkin-seed broth with tender pork — a completely different pot from red pozole, herbal and tangy rather than deep and dried-chilli-based.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
white onion, half quartered and half finely chopped

ingredients.note: canned hominy is sold in a few specialty Asian/Western grocers in Manila; dried hominy soaked and boiled overnight is the closer substitute if you can't find it
look for fresh tomatillo at specialty produce stalls or use canned tomatillo; in a pinch, substitute unripe green tomatoes plus extra lime juice for tartness
siling haba works, though it's milder — add a whole siling labuyo per person's taste if you want more heat

steps: Simmer the pork with the quartered onion and 2 garlic cloves in the water for about 1 hour, skimming foam, until the meat is tender. Strain and reserve the broth; keep the pork in a bowl.
Boil the tomatillos, poblanos and serranos in a separate small pot of water for 8 minutes until soft, then drain.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet, stirring constantly, until they puff and start to pop, then set aside to cool.
Blend the boiled tomatillos, poblanos, serranos, remaining garlic, half the toasted pumpkin seeds, cilantro and romaine leaves with a cup of the reserved broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the green purée for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens slightly and smells cooked rather than raw.
Add the remaining broth, the hominy and the cooked pork; simmer uncovered 20 minutes so the flavors come together.
Grind the remaining pumpkin seeds and stir half into the pot to thicken the broth slightly; taste and season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and let everyone garnish their own with chopped onion, radish, shredded cabbage, oregano, lime and the remaining ground pumpkin seeds.
tips: Fry the blended green sauce properly before adding broth — this step, called 'frying the base', is what stops pozole verde from tasting raw and grassy.
recipes.kidNote: The serrano chillies give this a real kick — for the kids' bowls, ladle broth before the chillies are blended in, or simply serve theirs with no chilli-forward garnish and keep sliced fresh chilli as a table topping for adults.
recipes.nutritionNote: Hominy and pumpkin seeds make this a good source of fibre alongside the pork protein; skim excess fat from the pork broth before serving to keep it lighter.

fil.description: Guerrero-style na hominy soup sa maliwanag na tomatillo, poblano, at pumpkin-seed broth with malambot na baboy — ibang klaseng pot kaysa red pozole, herbal at maasim imbes na malalim at dried-chilli-based.
ingredients: pork shoulder, hiwain nang malalaking chunks
white onion, half hiwain nang four parts at half tinadtad nang pino
raw pumpkin seeds, tinanggalan ng balat
steps: I-simmer ang baboy with quartered onion at 2 garlic cloves sa water for about 1 hour, tanggalin ang foam, hanggang lumambot ang karne. Salain at itabi ang broth; ilagay ang baboy sa bowl.
Pakuluan ang tomatillos, poblanos, at serranos sa separate small pot of water for 8 minutes hanggang lumambot, tapos i-drain.
I-toast ang pumpkin seeds sa dry skillet, haluin nang tuloy-tuloy, hanggang mag-puff at magsimulang pumutok, tapos itabi para lumamig.
I-blend ang pinakuluang tomatillos, poblanos, serranos, natitirang bawang, half ng toasted pumpkin seeds, cilantro, at romaine leaves with 1 cup ng itinabing broth hanggang smooth.
Painitin ang oil sa wide pot tapos iprito ang green purée for about 5 minutes, haluin madalas, hanggang bahagyang dumilim at maamoy niluto imbes na hilaw.
Idagdag ang natitirang broth, hominy, at lutong baboy; i-simmer nang walang takip for 20 minutes para magsama ang lasa.
Gilingin ang natitirang pumpkin seeds at ihalo ang half sa pot para bahagyang lumapot ang broth; tikman at timplahan ng asin.
Isandok sa bowls tapos hayaang mag-garnish ang bawat isa ng sarili nila with tinadtad na onion, radish, shredded cabbage, oregano, lime, at natitirang ground pumpkin seeds.
tips: Iprito nang maayos ang blended green sauce bago idagdag ang broth — itong step na tinatawag na 'frying the base' ang siyang pumipigil sa pozole verde na lumasang hilaw at grassy.
fil.kidNote: Talagang may anghang mula sa serrano chillies — para sa bowls ng mga bata, isandok ang broth bago i-blend ang chillies, o ihain na lang ang sa kanila nang walang chilli-forward na garnish at itago na lang ang hiniwang fresh chilli as table topping para sa adults.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang source ng fibre ang hominy at pumpkin seeds kasama ang protein ng baboy; alisin ang excess fat sa pork broth bago ihain para gumaan.

recipes.title: Red Pozole
recipes.description: Pork and hominy simmered in a deep guajillo-ancho broth and finished at the table with cabbage, radish and lime, the celebration soup for birthdays and Mexican Independence Day.

ingredients.item: pork spare ribs or baby back ribs
ingredients.note: or use all pork shoulder if ribs aren't available
cacahuazintle hominy sold canned or frozen at Latin/specialty grocers online in Manila; canned white corn kernels are a last-resort substitute though the texture differs
order dried guajillo and ancho chiles from a Mexican/Latin specialty grocer online if a local market doesn't carry them; they keep for months dried
table-only garnish, this is where the real heat is added; keep it off the kids' bowls entirely and let each adult spoon in their own

steps: Combine the pork shoulder, ribs, quartered onion and whole garlic cloves in a large pot with the water; bring to a boil, skim the foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is fork-tender.
Lift out the meat, discard the bones and any large fat, shred or chunk the meat, and return it to the strained broth.
Meanwhile, soak the guajillo and ancho chiles in a bowl of hot water 20-25 minutes until soft and pliable.
Drain the chiles and blend them with the sauce garlic, oregano and a cup of the broth until completely smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet, pour in the chile puree, and simmer 10 minutes, stirring often as it will splatter, until it deepens in color.
Strain the chile sauce into the pot of broth and meat to keep the pozole silky, add the drained hominy, and simmer 20-30 minutes until the hominy is tender.
Season with salt, keeping the pot itself mild; do not add chile piquin to the pot.
Ladle into deep bowls and let everyone garnish their own portion with cabbage, onion, radish and lime, adding crushed piquin or hot salsa only to the bowls that want it.
tips: This is a weekend project; the broth alone needs 2 to 2.5 hours, so start it in the morning for an evening meal.
Straining the chile puree into the broth removes the tough chile skins and keeps the pozole smooth rather than gritty.
recipes.kidNote: Keep the pot's chile base to guajillo and ancho only, it's warm, not fiery, and put the crushed chile piquin and any hot salsa out as table garnishes so each person, including the kids, spoons in their own heat.
recipes.nutritionNote: A hearty, protein-rich stew with fiber from the hominy; load up the table-side cabbage and radish to round it into a fuller vegetable serving.

source.name: Cooks Without Borders (Mely Martinez's Pozole Rojo)

fil.description: Pork at hominy na ni-simmer sa deep guajillo-ancho broth tapos tinatapos sa table with cabbage, radish at lime, ito ang celebration soup para sa birthdays at Mexican Independence Day.
ingredients: pork spare ribs o baby back ribs
guajillo chiles, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
ancho chiles, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
steps: Pagsamahin ang pork shoulder, ribs, quartered onion at whole garlic cloves sa large pot kasama ang tubig; pakuluin, alisin ang foam, tapos hinaan sa gentle simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours hanggang maging fork-tender ang karne.
Alisin ang karne, itapon ang bones at malalaking taba, i-shred o i-chunk ang karne, tapos ibalik sa strained broth.
Samantala, ibabad ang guajillo at ancho chiles sa bowl ng hot water for 20-25 minutes hanggang lumambot at maging pliable.
I-drain ang chiles tapos i-blend kasama ang bawang, oregano at isang cup ng broth hanggang completely smooth.
Painitin ang oil sa skillet, ibuhos ang chile puree, tapos i-simmer for 10 minutes, haluin madalas dahil magsi-splatter ito, hanggang dumilim ang kulay.
I-strain ang chile sauce papunta sa pot ng broth at karne para manatiling silky ang pozole, idagdag ang drained hominy, tapos i-simmer for 20-30 minutes hanggang lumambot ang hominy.
Timplahan ng asin, panatilihing mild ang pot mismo; wag maglagay ng chile piquin sa pot.
Isalok sa deep bowls tapos hayaang mag-garnish ang bawat isa ng sarili nilang portion with cabbage, onion, radish at lime, idagdag lang ang crushed piquin o hot salsa sa bowls na gusto nito.
tips: Weekend project ito; ang broth lang mismo kailangan ng 2 to 2.5 hours, kaya simulan sa umaga kung para sa hapunan.
Ang pag-strain ng chile puree papunta sa broth ay nag-aalis ng matigas na balat ng chile at pinapanatiling smooth ang pozole instead na gritty.
fil.kidNote: Panatilihing guajillo at ancho lang ang chile base ng pot, medyo warm lang ito, hindi fiery, tapos ilagay na lang ang crushed chile piquin at anumang hot salsa bilang table garnishes para bawat isa, kasama ang mga bata, sarili nilang isasalok ang gustong anghang.
fil.nutritionNote: Hearty at protein-rich na stew with fiber galing sa hominy; magdagdag ng table-side cabbage at radish para maging mas complete ang vegetable serving.

recipes.title: Roasted Poblano Strips in Cream
recipes.description: Roasted poblano strips simmered in a light garlic cream with sweet corn, a mild, silky side dish or taco filling found on nearly every central Mexican comedor menu.

ingredients.note: fresh, frozen or canned and drained
or sour cream thinned with a little milk

steps: Char the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under a hot broiler, turning, until blackened all over.
Seal the charred peppers in a plastic bag or covered bowl for 10 minutes to steam, then rub off the skin under cool running water.
Remove the stems and seeds, then slice the peppers into thin strips.
Heat the oil or butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and translucent, 4-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and corn and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the poblano strips and cook 2-3 minutes to combine the flavors.
Lower the heat, stir in the crema and salt, and simmer gently 3-4 minutes until warmed through; do not boil hard or the crema can split.
Scatter with cheese if using and serve warm as a side or tortilla filling.
tips: Poblanos vary in heat from pepper to pepper; taste a small piece after roasting, and if a batch runs spicier than expected, add extra crema and corn to mellow it for the kids' plates.
recipes.nutritionNote: Vegetable-forward with real fiber from the peppers and corn; the cream and cheese add richness, so keep this a side rather than the main dish, or thin the crema with milk for a lighter version.

fil.description: Roasted poblano strips na ni-simmer sa light garlic cream na may sweet corn, isang mild at silky side dish o taco filling na makikita sa halos lahat ng central Mexican comedor menu.
steps: I-char ang poblanos directly over gas flame o under hot broiler, i-turn, hanggang mag-itim all over.
Ilagay ang charred peppers sa plastic bag o covered bowl for 10 minutes para mag-steam, tapos kuskusin ang balat under cool running water.
Alisin ang tangkay at buto, tapos hiwain ang peppers into thin strips.
Painitin ang oil o butter sa skillet sa medium heat at lutuin ang onion hanggang lumambot at translucent, 4-5 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang at corn at lutuin for 2 minutes.
Ihalo ang poblano strips at lutuin for 2-3 minutes para mag-combine ang flavors.
Hinaan ang apoy, ihalo ang crema at asin, at i-simmer nang mahinay for 3-4 minutes hanggang uminit; wag pakuluin nang malakas kundi mag-split ang crema.
Budburan ng cheese kung gagamitin at ihain mainit as side o tortilla filling.
tips: Iba-iba ang anghang ng poblanos per pepper; tikman ang maliit na piraso after roasting, at kung mas maanghang than expected ang batch, magdagdag ng extra crema at corn para mas mellow para sa plato ng mga bata.
fil.nutritionNote: Vegetable-forward with real fiber from the peppers and corn; nagdadagdag ang cream at cheese ng richness, kaya panatilihin itong side kesa main dish, o i-thin ang crema with milk for lighter version.

recipes.title: Sopa de Lima
recipes.description: A Yucatecan chicken soup perfumed with sour lima citrus and a light tomato-pepper sofrito, finished with crisp fried tortilla strips for crunch.

ingredients.note: Yucatecan lima fruit isn't sold here; use fresh calamansi or a mix of lime and a little orange zest for the same sour-floral note
labuyo is far hotter per gram than habanero but similar in kick — use half a piece, kept whole, and taste before adding more

steps: Simmer the chicken thighs in the broth for 25 minutes until cooked through, then lift out, shred the meat, and set the broth aside.
Heat the oil in a soup pot and sauté the onion and bell pepper until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute, then stir in the tomatoes and oregano and cook until the tomatoes break down, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the reserved broth and bring to a simmer for 10 minutes so the flavors combine.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and stir in the lima or calamansi juice; taste and adjust the sourness and salt.
Meanwhile, fry the tortilla strips in hot oil until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Drop the whole habanero into the pot just before serving for aroma without heat, and remove it before ladling if no one wants it fiery.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with crisp tortilla strips and avocado slices.
recipes.kidNote: The habanero stays whole and unbroken in the broth purely for aroma; fish it out before serving the kids their bowls so there's no risk of it bursting into their portion.
recipes.nutritionNote: A light broth-based soup with lean chicken and vegetables; the fried tortilla strips add most of the fat, so go easy on those for a lighter bowl.

fil.description: Yucatecan na chicken soup na may amoy ng maasim na lima citrus at magaan na tomato-pepper sofrito, tinapusan ng crisp fried tortilla strips para sa crunch.
steps: I-simmer ang chicken thighs sa broth for 25 minutes hanggang maluto, tapos alisin, i-shred ang karne, at itabi ang broth.
Painitin ang oil sa soup pot at igisa ang onion at bell pepper hanggang lumambot, mga 5 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang at lutuin for 1 minute, tapos ihalo ang tomatoes at oregano at lutuin hanggang malusaw ang tomatoes, mga 5 minutes.
Ibuhos ang itinabing broth tapos i-simmer for 10 minutes para magsama ang lasa.
Ibalik ang shredded chicken sa pot tapos ihalo ang lima o calamansi juice; tikman at ayusin ang asim at asin.
Samantala, iprito ang tortilla strips sa hot oil hanggang golden at crisp, tapos i-drain sa paper towels.
Ilagay ang buong habanero sa pot bago mag-serve para sa amoy nang walang anghang, tapos alisin bago isandok kung walang gustong maanghang.
Isandok ang soup sa bowls tapos lagyan ng crisp tortilla strips at avocado slices.
fil.kidNote: Nananatiling buo at hindi nasisira ang habanero sa broth para sa amoy lang; kunin ito bago ihain sa mga bata para walang risk na pumutok sa portion nila.
fil.nutritionNote: Light na broth-based soup with lean na manok at vegetables; ang fried tortilla strips ang may pinakamaraming fat, kaya konti lang doon kung gusto mong mas light ang bowl.

recipes.title: Sopes de Chorizo
recipes.description: Thick hand-pressed masa cakes with pinched-up edges, griddled then fried and topped with refried beans, crumbled chorizo, potato, lettuce, and crema — a mercado stall classic.

ingredients.note: nixtamalised masa harina (Maseca brand) is carried by Mexican-goods importers and some supermarkets' international aisle; don't substitute rice flour or cornstarch
or use coarsely chopped longganiza with a pinch of cumin and a splash of vinegar if Mexican chorizo isn't available

ingredients.item: vegetable oil, for frying the sopes

steps: Mix the masa harina with salt and warm water, kneading until a soft, crack-free dough forms; cover with a damp cloth.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and pat each into a thick disc about 8cm wide and 1cm thick.
Cook the discs on a hot dry griddle for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly speckled but not fully browned.
While still warm, pinch up the edge of each disc with your fingers to form a small raised wall, then set aside to cool slightly.
Crumble the chorizo into a skillet over medium heat and cook until rendered and browned, about 6-8 minutes, then stir in the diced potato.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet and fry each sope shell, wall-side up, for about 1 minute until the base crisps.
Spread each fried sope with refried beans, top with the chorizo-potato mixture, lettuce, queso fresco, and a drizzle of crema.
Serve immediately with salsa roja on the side.
tips: Keep the dough covered with a damp cloth while you work — masa dries out and cracks fast.
Pinch the walls while the disc is still warm; once it cools it won't hold the shape.
recipes.kidNote: Keep the salsa roja off the kids' sopes and pass it at the table so each person spoons on their own heat — the chorizo itself is only mildly spiced.
recipes.nutritionNote: A hearty combination of fried masa, pork, and cheese; balance with the shredded lettuce and go light on the crema.

fil.description: Makapal na hand-pressed masa cakes na may pinched-up edges, ni-griddle tapos pinrito at nilagyan ng refried beans, durog na chorizo, potato, lettuce, at crema — classic mula sa mercado stall.
steps: Haluin ang masa harina with asin at warm water, mashin hanggang maging soft at walang crack ang dough; takpan ng damp cloth.
Hatiin ang dough into 8 balls tapos i-flatten ang bawat isa into thick disc na mga 8cm wide at 1cm thick.
Lutuin ang discs sa hot dry griddle for 2-3 minutes per side hanggang medyo speckled pero hindi pa fully browned.
Habang mainit pa, pisilin ang gilid ng bawat disc gamit ang daliri para makagawa ng maliit na raised wall, tapos itabi muna para lumamig nang kaunti.
Durugin ang chorizo papunta sa skillet sa medium heat tapos lutuin hanggang mag-render at mag-brown, mga 6-8 minutes, tapos ihalo ang diniced na potato.
Painitin ang oil sa wide skillet tapos iprito ang bawat sope shell, wall-side up, for about 1 minute hanggang mag-crisp ang base.
Pahiran ang bawat fried sope ng refried beans, lagyan ng chorizo-potato mixture, lettuce, queso fresco, at drizzle ng crema.
Ihain agad with salsa roja sa gilid.
tips: Panatilihing takip ang dough ng damp cloth habang ginagawa mo — mabilis matuyo at mag-crack ang masa.
Pisilin ang walls habang mainit pa ang disc; kapag lumamig na, hindi na siya magho-hold ng shape.
fil.kidNote: Huwag lagyan ng salsa roja ang sopes ng mga bata, ipasa na lang sa table para bawat isa magdagdag ng sariling anghang — banayad lang naman ang spice ng chorizo mismo.
fil.nutritionNote: Heavy combination ng fried masa, baboy, at cheese; i-balance with shredded lettuce at konti lang sa crema.

recipes.title: Tacos al Pastor
recipes.description: Thin pork slices marinated in a toasted guajillo-achiote adobo with pineapple, seared hot until charred at the edges and piled onto warm corn tortillas.

ingredients.item: dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
ingredients.note: or order dried guajillo online from a Mexican-goods importer; in a pinch use 2 tbsp mild chili powder plus 1 tsp smoked paprika

ingredients.item: dried ancho chile, stemmed and seeded
ingredients.note: if unavailable, add one extra guajillo instead
look for achiote paste at a Mexican grocer, or mix 2 tbsp atsuete/annatto powder with a little oil and vinegar
regular dried oregano works if Mexican oregano isn't available

steps: Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry pan for about 30 seconds per side, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the soaked chiles with the achiote paste, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin, and salt until smooth.
Coat the pork slices in the adobo, cover, and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat a griddle or heavy skillet until very hot and sear the pork in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Chop the seared pork into small pieces and toss with the chopped pineapple.
Warm the tortillas on the same hot pan for about 20 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the pork and pineapple, then top with onion, cilantro, and salsa.
tips: Marinate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight — that unattended time isn't counted in the cook time above.
A very hot, uncrowded pan matters more than a spit; crowded meat steams instead of charring.
recipes.kidNote: Blend the marinade without any extra chile de árbol and keep the table salsa off the kids' plates — they still get the smoky achiote and pineapple flavour without the heat. Put the arbol salsa on the table for the adults to add themselves.
recipes.nutritionNote: Rich in protein with moderate fat from the pork's natural marbling; balance the plate with the pineapple, shredded cabbage, or a simple salad.

fil.description: Manipis na hiwa ng baboy na ni-marinate sa toasted guajillo-achiote adobo may pineapple, sinunog nang mainit hanggang mag-char sa gilid, tapos ipinatong sa warm corn tortillas.
ingredients: guajillo chiles, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
ancho chile, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
steps: I-toast ang guajillo at ancho chiles sa dry pan for about 30 seconds per side, tapos ibabad sa hot water for 15 minutes hanggang lumambot.
I-blend ang nabababad na chiles kasama ang achiote paste, pineapple juice, vinegar, bawang, oregano, cumin, at asin hanggang maging smooth.
I-coat ang hiniwang baboy sa adobo, takpan, tapos i-marinate sa fridge for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Painitin ang griddle o heavy skillet hanggang sobrang init, tapos i-sear ang baboy in batches for 2-3 minutes per side hanggang mag-char sa gilid at maluto na.
Tadtarin ang naiprito na baboy nang maliliit, tapos haluin with tinadtad na pineapple.
I-warm ang tortillas sa parehong mainit na pan for about 20 seconds per side.
Lagyan ng baboy at pineapple ang tortillas, tapos budburan ng onion, cilantro, at salsa.
tips: I-marinate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight — 'yung oras na 'yon hindi kasama sa cook time sa taas.
Mas importante ang sobrang init at hindi masikip na pan kaysa spit; kapag masikip ang karne, na-steam lang siya imbes na mag-char.
fil.kidNote: I-blend ang marinade na walang extra chile de árbol at huwag lagyan ng table salsa ang plato ng mga bata — makukuha pa rin nila 'yung smoky achiote at pineapple flavor pero walang anghang. Ilagay na lang sa table ang arbol salsa para sa mga adults na magdagdag mismo.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa protein with moderate fat mula sa natural marbling ng baboy; i-balance ang plato with pineapple, shredded cabbage, o simpleng salad.

recipes.title: Tacos de Carnitas
recipes.description: Pork shoulder simmered low and slow in its own fat with citrus, garlic, and spices until fork-tender, then crisped in the pan for tacos with soft and crackly bits in every bite.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into large chunks

ingredients.note: use vegetable oil if lard isn't available

steps: Season the pork chunks generously with salt, pepper, oregano, and cumin.
Place the pork in a heavy pot with the garlic, onion, orange halves, bay leaves, and lard, and add just enough water to almost cover the meat.
Simmer uncovered over low heat for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the pork is fork-tender and the liquid has mostly evaporated.
Let the fat render out and fry the pork in it for the last 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally, until the edges turn crisp and golden.
Discard the orange halves and bay leaves, then shred the pork with two forks, keeping some of the crispy pieces whole.
Warm the tortillas on a hot dry pan for about 20 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the pork and top with chopped onion, cilantro, and salsa verde.
tips: Resist covering the pot — the liquid needs to evaporate so the meat can fry in its own rendered fat.
Leftover carnitas keep refrigerated for 3 days and reheat crisp in a dry skillet.
recipes.nutritionNote: High in protein and rendered fat; serve with a squeeze of lime and a crunchy cabbage or radish salad to lighten the plate.

fil.description: Pork shoulder na ni-simmer nang low and slow sa sarili niyang fat with citrus, bawang, at spices hanggang fork-tender, tapos pinacrisp sa pan for tacos na may soft at crackly bits sa bawat kagat.
ingredients: pork shoulder, hiwain nang malalaking chunks
white onion, hiwain nang four parts
steps: Timplahan nang generous ang pork chunks ng asin, pepper, oregano, at cumin.
Ilagay ang baboy sa heavy pot kasama ang bawang, onion, orange halves, bay leaves, at lard, tapos lagyan ng water na halos makatakip sa karne.
I-simmer nang walang takip sa low heat for about 2 hours, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang fork-tender na ang baboy at halos naevaporate na ang liquid.
Hayaang lumabas ang fat tapos iprito ang baboy dito for the last 15-20 minutes, baliktarin paminsan-minsan, hanggang mag-crisp at golden ang gilid.
Alisin ang orange halves at bay leaves, tapos i-shred ang baboy gamit ang two forks, iwan buo ang ibang crispy pieces.
I-warm ang tortillas sa hot dry pan for about 20 seconds per side.
Lagyan ng baboy ang tortillas tapos budburan ng tinadtad na onion, cilantro, at salsa verde.
tips: Huwag takpan ang pot — kailangan maevaporate ang liquid para maiprito ang karne sa sarili niyang rendered fat.
Pwedeng i-refrigerate ang leftover carnitas for 3 days at pag-init ulit sa dry skillet para maging crisp ulit.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa protein at rendered fat; ihain with squeeze of lime at crunchy cabbage o radish salad para gumaan ang plato.

recipes.title: Tlacoyos
recipes.description: Oval masa cakes stuffed with mashed beans, griddled until crisp-edged, and topped with nopales, cheese, and salsa — a central Mexican market breakfast staple.

ingredients.note: nixtamalised masa harina (Maseca brand) from a Mexican-goods importer; don't substitute plain cornstarch or rice flour

ingredients.item: cooked pinto or black beans, drained

ingredients.note: cactus is rarely available in Manila — substitute diced steamed green beans, or simply leave it out

steps: Heat the oil in a small pan, cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the beans and mash into a thick, spreadable paste; season with salt and let cool.
Mix the masa harina with salt and warm water, kneading until a soft dough forms that doesn't crack at the edges.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and flatten each into a small disc.
Place a spoonful of the mashed beans in the centre of each disc, fold the masa over the filling, and pinch closed.
Gently shape each stuffed ball into an oval about 1.5cm thick, patting to seal any cracks.
Cook on a hot dry griddle for 4-5 minutes per side until lightly charred and cooked through.
Top each tlacoyo with nopales, queso fresco, onion, and cilantro.
Serve with salsa verde on the side.
tips: Seal the edges well or the bean filling will burst out onto the griddle.
Tlacoyos freeze well after cooking; reheat straight from frozen on a dry pan.
recipes.nutritionNote: A fibre- and protein-rich vegetarian meal from the beans and corn masa; go easy on the cheese if serving as a main rather than a snack.

fil.description: Oval na masa cakes na tinapunan ng mashed beans, ni-griddle hanggang crisp ang gilid, tapos nilagyan ng nopales, cheese, at salsa — staple breakfast sa central Mexican market.
ingredients: lutong pinto o black beans, sinala
steps: Painitin ang oil sa small pan, lutuin ang bawang for 30 seconds, tapos idagdag ang beans at durugin into thick, spreadable paste; timplahan ng asin at hayaang lumamig.
Haluin ang masa harina with asin at warm water, mashin hanggang maging soft ang dough na hindi nagc-crack sa gilid.
Hatiin ang dough into 8 portions tapos i-flatten ang bawat isa into small disc.
Ilagay ang isang kutsarang mashed beans sa gitna ng bawat disc, itiklop ang masa sa filling, tapos pisilin para masarhan.
Dahan-dahang hubugin ang bawat stuffed ball into oval na mga 1.5cm thick, i-pat para masarhan ang mga crack.
Lutuin sa hot dry griddle for 4-5 minutes per side hanggang medyo mag-char at maluto na.
Lagyan ang bawat tlacoyo ng nopales, queso fresco, onion, at cilantro.
Ihain with salsa verde sa gilid.
tips: Siguraduhing nasarhan nang maayos ang gilid kundi lalabas ang beans sa griddle.
Maganda i-freeze ang tlacoyos pagkatapos lutuin; pwede i-reheat straight from frozen sa dry pan.
fil.nutritionNote: Fibre- at protein-rich na vegetarian meal mula sa beans at corn masa; konti lang sa cheese kung ihahain as main imbes na snack.

recipes.title: Tortilla Soup
recipes.description: A pasilla-tomato broth ladled over crisp fried tortilla strips and topped with avocado, cheese and crema, the soup nearly every Mexico City kitchen serves before the main course.

ingredients.item: corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
vegetable oil, for frying the tortillas

ingredients.note: dried pasilla sold by Mexican/Latin specialty importers online in Manila; substitute 1 ancho chile if unavailable
or sour cream thinned with milk

steps: Fry the tortilla strips in batches in the hot oil until crisp and golden, about 2 minutes; drain on paper towels and set aside.
Soak the pasilla chile in hot water 10 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and softened pasilla until completely smooth.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot over medium heat, pour in the blended sauce, and cook, stirring, 8-10 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Add the broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer 10 minutes and season with salt.
Just before serving, divide the fried tortilla strips among bowls and ladle the hot broth over them so they stay crisp at the table.
Top with avocado, queso fresco and a drizzle of crema, with lime wedges alongside.
tips: Add the tortilla strips to the bowl last, always, or they turn soggy sitting in the broth.
The salsa base can be made a day ahead and refrigerated; fry the tortillas fresh right before serving.
recipes.nutritionNote: A light tomato-based broth; keep the fried tortilla strips and crema portions modest for a lighter bowl, or bake the strips instead of frying for less oil.

source.name: 196 Flavors (recipe validated by Mely Martinez of Mexico in My Kitchen)

fil.description: Pasilla-tomato broth na binuhos sa crisp fried tortilla strips at topped with avocado, cheese at crema, ang soup na halos lahat ng kusina sa Mexico City ay iniihain bago ang main course.
ingredients: corn tortillas, hiwain into thin strips
pasilla chile, tanggalan ng tangkay at buto
steps: I-fry ang tortilla strips in batches sa hot oil hanggang crisp at golden, mga 2 minutes; i-drain sa paper towels at itabi.
I-soak ang pasilla chile sa hot water for 10 minutes hanggang lumambot, tapos i-drain.
I-blend ang tomatoes, onion, bawang at softened pasilla hanggang completely smooth.
Painitin ang 1 tablespoon oil sa pot sa medium heat, ibuhos ang blended sauce, at lutuin, haluin, for 8-10 minutes hanggang dumilim at lumapot.
Idagdag ang broth, pakuluin, tapos hinaan sa simmer for 10 minutes at timplahan ng asin.
Bago ihain, hatiin ang fried tortilla strips sa bowls at isabit ang mainit na broth dito para manatiling crisp sa table.
Topping ng avocado, queso fresco at drizzle ng crema, with lime wedges sa tabi.
tips: Idagdag ang tortilla strips sa bowl last, palagi, kundi magiging soggy ito.
Pwedeng gawin ang salsa base isang araw bago at i-refrigerate, tapos i-fry ang tortillas fresh right before serving.
fil.nutritionNote: Light na tomato-based broth; panatilihing modest ang fried tortilla strips at crema portions para mas light ang bowl, o i-bake na lang ang strips instead of pag-frito para less oil.

recipes.title: Veracruz-Style Fish
recipes.description: White fish fillets gently simmered in a Spanish-influenced tomato sauce with olives, capers and pickled jalapenos, Veracruz's coastal answer to Mediterranean flavors landing on Mexican shores.

ingredients.item: white fish fillets, about 150 g each
ingredients.note: red snapper (huachinango) is traditional; tilapia or cream dory are easy local substitutes
or use 1 can (400 g) whole peeled tomatoes, more reliable off-season
jalapenos en escabeche; or use pickled banana peppers if unavailable

ingredients.item: ground cinnamon or a pinch of nutmeg

steps: Season the fish fillets with lime juice and salt, then set aside while you make the sauce.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, deep skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant, then stir in the chopped tomatoes, olives, capers, pickled jalapenos, bay leaf and cinnamon.
Simmer the sauce uncovered 10-12 minutes until it thickens and loses its raw-tomato smell.
Nestle the fish fillets into the sauce, spooning some sauce over the top, cover, and simmer gently 8-10 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Taste and adjust salt, then remove the bay leaf.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve straight from the pan with white rice.
tips: Simmer the fish gently; a hard boil will break the fillets apart before they finish cooking.
Make the sauce up to a day ahead, it deepens in flavor overnight, and only poach the fish just before serving.
For the kids' plates, spoon sauce around the jalapeno slices rather than over them, or fish the slices out before serving.
recipes.nutritionNote: Lean white fish with tomatoes and olive oil is a heart-healthy combination; watch the sodium from olives and capers and skip added salt at the table.

fil.description: White fish fillets na ni-simmer nang dahan-dahan sa Spanish-influenced tomato sauce with olives, capers at pickled jalapenos, ito ang coastal answer ng Veracruz sa Mediterranean flavors na dumating sa Mexican shores.
ingredients: lime, kinuha ang juice, para sa fish
steps: Timplahan ang fish fillets ng lime juice at asin, tapos itabi muna habang ginagawa ang sauce.
Painitin ang olive oil sa wide, deep skillet sa medium heat tapos lutuin ang onion hanggang lumambot, mga 4 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang tapos lutuin for 1 minute hanggang umamoy maganda, saka ihalo ang chopped tomatoes, olives, capers, pickled jalapenos, bay leaf at cinnamon.
I-simmer ang sauce nang bukas for 10-12 minutes hanggang lumapot at mawala ang amoy ng raw tomato.
Ilagay ang fish fillets sa loob ng sauce, budburan ng kaunting sauce sa ibabaw, takpan, tapos i-simmer nang dahan-dahan for 8-10 minutes hanggang mag-flake nang madali ang fish.
Tikman at ayusin ang asin, tapos alisin ang bay leaf.
Budburan ng parsley tapos ihain straight from the pan with white rice.
tips: I-simmer nang dahan-dahan ang fish; kapag hard boil, mawawasak ang fillets bago pa matapos maluto.
Pwede gawin ang sauce up to a day ahead, mas lumalalim ang lasa overnight, tapos i-poach na lang ang fish just before serving.
Para sa plato ng mga bata, ilagay ang sauce sa paligid ng jalapeno slices instead na sa ibabaw nito, o kunin na lang ang slices bago ihain.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang lean white fish with tomatoes at olive oil ay heart-healthy combination; bantayan ang sodium mula sa olives at capers tapos wag nang magdagdag pa ng asin sa table.

recipes.title: Zucchini with Corn
recipes.description: Mexican zucchini and sweet corn sauteed with onion, tomato and a touch of chile, a quick everyday vegetable side that home cooks like Mely Martinez say they could eat daily.

ingredients.note: deseed for milder, or omit entirely for a fully mild pot
regular green zucchini is a close substitute
fresh off the cob is traditional; frozen or canned works too

steps: Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until translucent, 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and chile and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the diced zucchini and corn and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped tomatoes, cover, and cook 8-10 minutes until the zucchini is tender but not mushy and the tomatoes have broken down into a light sauce.
Uncover, season with salt, and simmer 2-3 minutes more to let any extra liquid evaporate.
Scatter with queso fresco if using and serve warm as a side, or spoon over rice for a light meal.
tips: Don't overcook the zucchini, it should still hold its shape; cut it into even pieces so it cooks at the same rate as the corn.
recipes.nutritionNote: A fiber- and vitamin-rich vegetable side that's naturally low in fat; a good way to get the kids eating vegetables since the corn sweetness balances the zucchini.

fil.description: Mexican zucchini at sweet corn na ginisa sa onion, kamatis at kaunting chile, isang mabilis na everyday vegetable side na sabi ng mga home cook gaya ni Mely Martinez ay puwede na nilang kainin araw-araw.
steps: Painitin ang oil sa wide skillet sa medium heat at lutuin ang onion hanggang translucent, 3 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang at chile at lutuin for 1 minute hanggang bumango.
Ihalo ang diced zucchini at corn at lutuin for 5 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan.
Idagdag ang chopped tomatoes, takpan, at lutuin for 8-10 minutes hanggang lumambot ang zucchini pero hindi mushy at mag-breakdown ang tomatoes into light sauce.
Buksan, timplahan ng asin, at i-simmer for 2-3 minutes more para mag-evaporate ang extra liquid.
Budburan ng queso fresco kung gagamitin at ihain mainit as side, o ilagay sa ibabaw ng rice for a light meal.
tips: Wag i-overcook ang zucchini, dapat hindi ito nawawalan ng shape; hiwain nang pantay para maluto sabay ng corn.
fil.nutritionNote: Fiber- at vitamin-rich na vegetable side na naturally low in fat; good way para makakain ng gulay ang mga bata kasi binabalance ng tamis ng corn ang zucchini.
